chapters.title: Chapter 861: An Asset
paragraphs: [The Red Devil’s Mercenary Group - Haunted Grounds - The Valley of Torture]
"Fuck... Fuck... Fuck..."
The Dark Elf cursed as he flew ahead of a team of four.
A couple of hours ago, they were a capable team of seventeen mercenaries.
However, after crossing paths with Kent, not only was their team reduced to four, but they also found themselves in one of the most dangerous parts of the Valley of Torture.
"You three, hurry before it catches up to us," the Dark Elf said, but his three teammates weren’t having a good time.

Of course, the Level 5 Spirit Lord that Adina fought with before the formation took them away held a cold look in his eyes and was determined to get close to the Dark Elf, not for any noble intentions.
He had warned his team about the dangers surrounding their mission, but none had listened.
The money allocated to the mission was so big that they lost their focus, and now, regardless of whether they lived or died, he knew they wouldn’t be able to return to being a team ever again.
Iver cursed his team leader in his heart but kept flying. Soon, the horror in the form of a bone dragon appeared in the distance, chasing after them.
Within a couple of seconds, it was upon them.
"We need to split up, or it will pick us all off in one go," Iver shouted. However, none liked the idea.
Obviously, no one liked the idea of becoming the bait.
The moment they split up, the bone dragon would pick one of them and chase after them. That would give the rest of the team some time to create distance between themselves and the dragon.
It was a good strategy, but at least one would have to die for the three to live.
"I won’t be dying for this stupid mission. So I’ll be going my separate way." Without hesitation, Iver dived to his left and separated himself from his teammates.

He didn’t even stop flying, knowing the only way out now was to get as far as he could from his team. Naturally, the moment Iver went his separate way, the Level 4 Spirit Lords also went their separate ways.
Thankfully, the dragon picked none of them; instead, it went after their leader, who was left to fend for himself against the Level 9 Spirit Lord Bone Dragon.
This couldn’t have been a better outcome. With his strength, he would keep the dragon occupied for a few minutes, allowing his team to get away.
[2,000 miles away from the Lightning Peak — Kent and Adina’s POV]
Kent and Adina had spent the last fourteen hours on the move, doing their best not to attract the attention of the beast lurking in the shadows.
With the tower aiding navigation, their movement was swift. However, they both knew it was only a matter of time before their luck ran out.
Even so, they were getting closer to their destination.
"Stop." Kent came to a sudden halt when he sensed something.
He grabbed Adina’s hand and led her away, moving calmly through the forest. A few minutes later, they stopped again, and Kent took out his sword.
They started moving again, but this time even more cautiously. Slowly, they stood behind a large stone. Kent moved to the side and sneaked out of his head.
"Well, I’ll be damned." A smile appeared on Kent’s face.
"What is it?" Adina asked, but to answer her question, Kent pulled her forward so she could see for herself.
"Is that—?"
"Yes. That is one of the guys who ambushed us. Looks like it’s time for some payback." An evil smile appeared on Kent’s face.
"Are we going to kill him?" Adina asked, but Kent shook his head.
"In Financial Accounting, we call some things assets. This bastard is now an indispensable asset, at least for now. So I’m going to work my magic on him."
"What is Financial Accounting?" Adina asked, catching Kent off guard.
He turned and looked at her with a smile on his face. "So that was your takeaway from all I said?"
"It will help me understand what we are about to do." Adina looked serious, thinking that Financial Accounting had a much deeper meaning.
Kent kept smiling, knowing humans can be silly sometimes, naming everything mysterious to mess with students’ heads.
"Don’t worry about it. It has no mysterious meaning in what is about to happen." Adina was reluctant, but she nodded. Kent smirked and turned back to Iver, who was wounded and bleeding on the ground.
He seemed not to have escaped the bone dragon unscathed.
’Tower, I want a rundown.’

⟦This person has a Tier 14 soul, so the master can’t use soul torture on him. However, there is an opening in his mind that I believe, with the right skillset, the master can get inside his mind and make him his bitch.⟧
"Wow, Tower, where did you learn that word from?" Kent smiled, hearing the tone the tower used.
⟦I grow and learn as the master grows.⟧
"Are you saying this is my fault?"
⟦The master is my teacher, so I can only follow the master’s teachings, even if he doesn’t know he was teaching me.⟧
"Tch." Kent chuckled and turned to Adina.
"Wait here, I will be back in a few seconds." Adina nodded and hid behind the stone while Kent blinked away.
Iver was bleeding from his chest and in so much pain that when Kent appeared behind him, he didn’t notice.
However, it was only for a moment before he noticed him. But by then, Kent was ready and gently tapped Iver’s forehead with his index finger.
His eyes rolled back, and then he froze.
"Now, why don’t we handle the main part?"
Kent activated his mind manipulation skill, and with no resistance whatsoever, he got inside Iver’s mind.
"Done."
Kent took a Tier 8 healing pill, put it in Iver’s mouth, before taking out the small flying boat that Lady Enzi had given him. He activated it and tossed Iver in.
He picked Adina up, and soon, they were several miles away.
He didn’t want to stay at the place where Iver’s blood had already started drawing the beast in. So they moved away.
A few minutes after they left, a Level 7 Spirit Lord beast appeared, and soon more followed, but Kent and Adina were long gone, now in possession of an asset that couldn’t have come at a better time.
[The Cave Where Kent and Adina Stayed — The Wandering Swordsman]
The red-skinned demon swordsman had managed to find the battlefield where the short battle between Kent and the Red Devil mercenaries had taken place.
Using his advanced senses, he was able to track the direction Kent and Adina had gone after the battle, so he followed the trail to the mountain cave.
"Looks like there are two of them," he muttered, entering the cave. However, just when he was being cocky, his senses picked up something, but things ended rather abruptly.
BOOM.
The mountain was reduced to nothing, and the Wandering Swordsman was sent flying several miles away, his body littered with injuries.

chapters.title: Chapter 862: Several Steps Ahead
paragraphs: [A few minutes before leaving the Cave – Kent’s POV]
“Wait for me outside,” Kent said to Adina, who nodded and walked out of the cave.

“Alright, time to get to work.” Kent took out some items he had purchased from the tower. With a tower that could get him almost anything, he saw an opportunity to make sure whoever follows their trail experiences a world of pain.
⟦I have to ask, master, what makes you think anyone would be able to pick up your trail and come here?⟧
Kent laughed. “You are still a green tower. Why do you think I fought those bastards? I did that just to leave my aura there.
Naturally, I could have used the [Rule Breaker] to cancel out my aura there and do the same for Adina. However, I chose to fight them with the main goal of leaving our aura behind.
Now, if you are looking for someone and see a battlefield, the first thing you would do is sense the various auras and follow the ones that got away.
Naturally, I know someone will come, and I intend to make them aware of who they are following. I wouldn’t want to make them think I am just some greenhouse flower.”
Kent smiled and started setting things up.
It took him a few minutes to set everything up.
Then he walked out of the cave.
Outside, he formed a hand seal, and a formation appeared over the mountain and slowly enveloped it.
“Let’s go.” Kent retrieved the small flying boat, and they hopped in.
[Before the Explosion]
Kent was directing the flying boat toward Lightning Peak, where they planned to stay for a few hours, perhaps a day, before continuing their journey.
Though their journey to the Lightning Peak was a smooth ride, he knew things would soon be chaotic, so he wanted them to have a much-needed rest before anything.
Suddenly, Kent slowed down the boat and smiled.
“Got your ass.”
The formation he had left around the mountain had just moved, and while he couldn’t see the person who had come, he felt the presence.
“Since you managed to pick up on our trail, then I can only slow you down for a few days.” The smile on his face turned evil.
“I really hope you are not standing at the center of the cave.” With that, Kent snapped his fingers, and several miles from them, it went boom.
[The Explosion]
The wandering demon swordsman, thanks to his arrogance, entered the cave with no care for who was waiting for him.
He was a level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator, so fearing someone he was told was only at level 3 Spirit Lord stage was just not something he planned on doing.
So he entered with his shoulders high, suspecting nothing.
He looked around but saw nothing.
However, just when he was about to use his senses like he should have from the start, he was already at the most dangerous impact zone.
He had no time to raise his defense, so the blast landed on him and sent him flying.
[Post Explosion]
The wandering demon swordsman landed hard on a large rock, shattering it upon impact. An agonizing pain erupted from his mouth.
The blast and impact were both painful, and judging by the cut-off leg, he would need a couple of days, perhaps a week, to regrow it.
As someone who has already formed a spiritual core and a Spirit Root, he could regrow body parts; therefore, he would need to expend some energy to regrow his leg.
“This bitch, I will be sure to cut your body into many parts even if it means I fail this mission,” the wandering demon swordsman said, sitting in lotus posture, and started cultivating.
“Fuck... I have to deal with the poison first.”
His anger boiled over, driving him to get things done much faster, so he would chase after Kent and Adina, whom he planned to kill in the most agonizing way possible.
[12,000 Miles Away from the Explosion Site – The Green Fang Mercenary Group]
One of the mercenary teams from Planet Menelaus was making their way through the valley when an explosion echoed several miles away from them.
“Was that an explosion?” a stone-faced demon asked.

“Definitely. I extended my sense several miles in that direction and felt the shockwave. We should check it out,” a dwarf with one horn on his forehead, wielding an axe, said, causing his team to nod.
“Team leader, what if it were a battle between two powerful beasts?” one of them asked.
“Relax, Dane, the explosion was enough to kill a Spirit Lord at the 5th level, so of course I wasn’t asking for us to get close to where the explosion happened.
We can scout and see if we can find any clues that will point us in the right direction.”
“Okay, leader.” They started moving in the direction of the explosion.
Naturally, this was all in Kent’s calculation.
When he left his aura behind, he made sure the only person who could sense it had to have a powerful sense.
This means he took into account the main person he planned on running from, namely the level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator, who would sense it.
Then he also made sure the explosion would do more than hurt the person. He wanted the explosion to be heard thousands of miles away and to draw the attention of all kinds.
At the moment, there were only two outcomes, and one of them was that the person who triggered the explosion died, which Kent knew they didn’t because he received no tower points.
So, since that wasn’t the case, then it could only mean the person still lives and is probably pissed.
Now, the outcome that somebody heard the explosion and came looking will come and meet a level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator who is probably angry and wants blood.
The rest will resolve itself.
“Why are you smiling?” Adina, who had been quiet on the trip, suddenly asked, looking at the smug smile on Kent’s face.
Kent turned and looked at her. “Let’s just say our biggest problem has been delayed for a few days. This adds to our advantage, and I plan on taking advantage of that to get far from here.”
“So your explosion worked.”
Kent wasn’t surprised when he heard her question. After all, she is a Spirit Lord; a mere trigger formation couldn’t escape her sight.
“Something like that. Now, we just have to get as far away as we can from this scum before using him for what I planned on using you for.”
Adina looked at Kent weirdly. “What were you planning on using me for?”
“Bait.”
“What?”

Kent smiled. “Don’t overreact. Where we are going has a Level 8 Spirit Lord. I planned on using you as bait to catch it. I had all plans set, and the risk level was one you wouldn’t have worried about.”
Adina bit her lips, a murderous look in her eyes as she looked at Kent. “What was the risk?”
Kent smiled, “Just 70%, but a 30% success rate is one I see as an absolute win.”
“You—”
Adina pointed at Kent, frustration bubbling in her eyes. However, she smirked and turned away from him, unsure if she could hold her anger if she kept staring at Kent’s face.

Though their journey to the Lightning Peak was a smooth ride, he knew things would soon be chaotic, so he wanted them to have a much-needed rest before anything.
Suddenly, Kent slowed down the boat and smiled.
“Got your ass.”
The formation he had left around the mountain had just moved, and while he couldn’t see the person who had come, he felt the presence.
“Since you managed to pick up on our trail, then I can only slow you down for a few days.” The smile on his face turned evil.
“I really hope you are not standing at the center of the cave.” With that, Kent snapped his fingers, and several miles from them, it went boom.
[The Explosion]
The wandering demon swordsman, thanks to his arrogance, entered the cave with no care for who was waiting for him.
He was a level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator, so fearing someone he was told was only at level 3 Spirit Lord stage was just not something he planned on doing.
So he entered with his shoulders high, suspecting nothing.
He looked around but saw nothing.
However, just when he was about to use his senses like he should have from the start, he was already at the most dangerous impact zone.
He had no time to raise his defense, so the blast landed on him and sent him flying.
[Post Explosion]
The wandering demon swordsman landed hard on a large rock, shattering it upon impact.
An agonizing pain erupted from his mouth.
The blast and impact were both painful, and judging by the cut-off leg, he would need a couple of days, perhaps a week, to regrow it.
As someone who has already formed a spiritual core and a Spirit Root, he could regrow body parts; therefore, he would need to expend some energy to regrow his leg.
“This bitch, I will be sure to cut your body into many parts even if it means I fail this mission,” the wandering demon swordsman said, sitting in lotus posture, and started cultivating.
“Fuck...
I have to deal with the poison first.”
His anger boiled over, driving him to get things done much faster, so he would chase after Kent and Adina, whom he planned to kill in the most agonizing way possible.
[12,000 Miles Away from the Explosion Site – The Green Fang Mercenary Group]
One of the mercenary teams from Planet Menelaus was making their way through the valley when an explosion echoed several miles away from them.
“Was that an explosion?” a stone-faced demon asked.
“Definitely.
I extended my sense several miles in that direction and felt the shockwave.
We should check it out,” a dwarf with one horn on his forehead, wielding an axe, said, causing his team to nod.
“Team leader, what if it were a battle between two powerful beasts?” one of them asked.
“Relax, Dane, the explosion was enough to kill a Spirit Lord at the 5th level, so of course I wasn’t asking for us to get close to where the explosion happened.
We can scout and see if we can find any clues that will point us in the right direction.”
“Okay, leader.” They started moving in the direction of the explosion.
Naturally, this was all in Kent’s calculation.
When he left his aura behind, he made sure the only person who could sense it had to have a powerful sense.
This means he took into account the main person he planned on running from, namely the level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator, who would sense it.
Then he also made sure the explosion would do more than hurt the person.
He wanted the explosion to be heard thousands of miles away and to draw the attention of all kinds.
At the moment, there were only two outcomes, and one of them was that the person who triggered the explosion died, which Kent knew they didn’t because he received no tower points.
So, since that wasn’t the case, then it could only mean the person still lives and is probably pissed.
Now, the outcome that somebody heard the explosion and came looking will come and meet a level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator who is probably angry and wants blood.
The rest will resolve itself.
“Why are you smiling?” Adina, who had been quiet on the trip, suddenly asked, looking at the smug smile on Kent’s face.
Kent turned and looked at her.
“Let’s just say our biggest problem has been delayed for a few days.
This adds to our advantage, and I plan on taking advantage of that to get far from here.”
“So your explosion worked.”
Kent wasn’t surprised when he heard her question.
After all, she is a Spirit Lord; a mere trigger formation couldn’t escape her sight.
“Something like that.
Now, we just have to get as far away as we can from this scum before using him for what I planned on using you for.”
Adina looked at Kent weirdly.
“What were you planning on using me for?”
“Bait.”
“What?”
Kent smiled.
“Don’t overreact.
Where we are going has a Level 8 Spirit Lord.
I planned on using you as bait to catch it.
I had all plans set, and the risk level was one you wouldn’t have worried about.”
Adina bit her lips, a murderous look in her eyes as she looked at Kent.
“What was the risk?”
Kent smiled, “Just 70%, but a 30% success rate is one I see as an absolute win.”
“You—”
Adina pointed at Kent, frustration bubbling in her eyes.
However, she smirked and turned away from him, unsure if she could hold her anger if she kept staring at Kent’s face.

chapters.title: Chapter 863: Getting Some Information
paragraphs: [Lightning Peak – Base of the Mountain]

“Let’s stay here for now. Tomorrow, after everything is set, we will climb to face the beast that lives here.” Kent retrieved a small tent and infused it with his energy. It inflated, and soon a large enough tent was set up.
He took out a Tier 12 Array that Alina had made for him. It could be used to conceal the presence of anything.
Kent activated it, and soon, the tent became invincible.

Kent carried the unconscious Iver inside and put him on one side of the tent. It was spacious enough for more than thirty people, so Adina was able to find a corner, making sure she was far from Kent.
Kent just chuckled when he saw that.
A few minutes later, he snapped his fingers, and Iver woke up with a throbbing headache.
“Get it all out, buddy. I have some stuff to ask you,” Kent said, looking at the panting young man whose mind was no longer his.
Kent could easily access his memories; however, he didn’t want to mess with his mind and accidentally turn Iver into an idiot, as he had a mission for him.
He wanted Iver to speak for himself, and since he had control over his mind, Kent knew he would speak like a parrot.
After 20 minutes, Iver managed to calm down a bit.
“First of all, tell me who you are,” Kent asked, and like he expected, Iver started to sing like a bird.
“My name is Iver Hvvyt Huip. I am from Planet Menelaus and a member of the Red Devils Mercenary Guild.”
“What was your mission?”
“We were instructed to intercept a lady who will be passing through here and bring her in dead or alive.”
“Who gave you the mission?”
“It came from the Incubus King from Planet Psyche.”
“What do you know about this Incubus King?” Kent wanted to know everything. The mission he was on was a delicate one, and as such, he wanted to know everything so he could plan well.
After all, the more information he has now, the better his future plans will be if the need arises.
“He is a Supreme King.”
Kent raised his brow, hearing something new. “A Supreme King. What does that mean?”
“A Supreme King is a king in a Supreme High World. Planet Psyche is a Supreme High World, so the king ruling over it is naturally a Supreme King.”
“I see.” Kent turned and looked at Adina, who was pretending she wasn’t listening to the conversation despite having her fist clenched so hard her palm had started bleeding.
“So, how many of you were sent after her, and if possible, tell me their power levels.”
Iver was more than happy to answer Kent. “Aside from us, ten other mercenary groups took the mission. Among the ten, we rank seventh in strength and last in number.

The top team is the Iron Brigade, a team of metal men, and the strongest in my world. The second team is made up of elves. They are dangerous and bloodthirsty by nature. Their leader is a half-Elf, half-Dark Elf.
As for the third team, all of them are assassins, so I don’t know much about them. All three top teams have a Level 9 Spirit Lord leader and two Level 8 Spirit Lords.”
Kent scratched the back of his head.

‘I am out of my league here,’ he had to admit. The mission was one he would have loved to spend more time on; however, he also knew that the more time he wasted, the closer the danger would get to him.
So he must hurry and send Adina on her way before perhaps risking his life.
“Tell me, is there a Level 2 Ascension stage cultivator also on this mission?”
Iver paused for a moment, unsure how to answer the question. However, upon thinking for a minute, he understood the question.
“If you are talking about the Wandering Demon Swordsman, then perhaps yes.”
“Wait, what did you say?” Kent moved in closer, almost killing Iver with his eyes.
“The Wandering Demon Swordsman.”
“I will be damned.” Kent laughed and sat back. “Looks like I didn’t come here by accident. There is a much higher calling that I must fulfill before leaving.”
All of a sudden, Kent felt like this mission had just gotten more interesting.
“Tell me more about this Wandering Demon Swordsman.”

“He is dangerous, very dangerous, in fact. I only learned about him when I found out he would be joining us on the mission. But from what I gathered, he is a Sword King who is almost touching the Heavenly Sword Energy to become a Sword Emperor.
He is a blood demon who preys on the blood of his kills, and while he is not from a Supreme High World, he has the power to go to one and perhaps roam it.

I even learned he killed a Sword Emperor and has been on the run ever since. There are many bounties on his head, but no one dares go against him, not even Sword Emperors after finding out he killed one of them.”
“So he is a big shot that everyone wants dead, but is afraid to face him. Am I right?”
Iver nodded to Kent’s question.
“The highest bounty on his head was issued by the Olive Sword Guild located in my world. The reward is one everyone would want, but nobody dares go against the Wandering Demon Swordsman.”
“I see.” Kent turned to Adina, who now seemed to have turned a little pale, hearing such a person was after her.
Kent smiled, “Looks like I will have to send you away to the Teleportation Mountain much faster. If there is such a person here, I can only greet him and see if we can have a lovely chat.”
Adina looked at him for a few minutes before asking, “You said your name is Kent, right?”
“The one and only.”
“Then are you perhaps Kent Madson?” Adina asked again, and Kent’s smile froze.
“I never told you my surname.”
“So you are Kent Madson,” Adina asked, and Kent stood up, looking at her weirdly. He didn’t know why she asked, but he intended to find out.
“Yes, I am Kent Madson.”
Adina didn’t say anything, but Iver spoke.
“So you are the one the entire universe is looking for.”
“Say what now?” Such a question took aback Kent.
“Oh, you didn’t know?” Adina chimed in. “Apparently, out of nowhere, a name—’ Kent Madson’—appeared on the Sword Dao Tablet, and ever since, everyone has been searching for you.
And in case you are not aware, the Sword Dao Tablet only records the names of people who have accomplished great feats on the path of the sword.
There are now fourteen names on it. The first thirteen are all legends who walked the path of the sword.

Now, your name has appeared on such a tablet, and while many masters are searching for you to become their disciples, powerful families and planets are also searching for you to either kill you or make you their pawn if they have the power.
It will be best if you stay low-key for a while. Trust me, you don’t want to become like me, always on the run.”
Adina spoke with a sigh in the end...

chapters.title: Chapter 864: Opening Up
paragraphs: Hearing Adina’s words, Kent was drawn into the danger his unknown accomplishment pulled him into. He immediately realised not everything is a good thing.
“If the entire universe is searching for me, then that means even gods and immortals are aware of me now, and they might even be involved in the search.
If that is the case, then I am fucked.”
The realization only made him look at Adina with a more concerned expression. “Are you being chased down by gods, too?”
Adina didn’t respond immediately.
She took a few breaths before she started to speak. “I am not being chased by gods. I am running because a Supreme wants my body.”
“What?”
Kent looked at Adina, expecting to see a pained look in her eyes. However, all he saw was determination. It was as if she had given in to the pain and was now looking to get out of it.
That is even more traumatizing when one looks at things from a much more neutral perspective.
She is but a mere Spirit Lord who a Supreme is chasing down. That wasn’t something that could be taken lightly. ‘It is even a miracle she is still alive and never gives up’
‘Who knows how long she had been on the run?’ Kent was unsure how to approach the conversation, as he had never expected Adina’s enemy to be a Supreme.
“Why does this Supreme need your body?” Kent eventually asked.
“Why else would a Supreme need my body if not for my Extreme Pure Yin Body Constitution?” Adina smiled weakly, a smile that contained her pain and anger.

“It turns out that being a succubus who inherited the Sin of Lust curse but managed to defy it by staying chaste has its downside, and mine came in the form of a heavenly constitution, one that got my entire clan killed.

So, well, being popular has its upsides, but trust me, the downsides are more than you can handle. So take my advice: as long as you don’t have the means to defend yourself against gods, never make everyone know your name or who you are.
You will regret it in the worst way possible.”
“Thanks for the advice, but don’t worry, I have everything under control.” Kent laughed, knowing that things wouldn’t be simple soon enough.
Of course, he planned to ensure his future was safe. No matter the odds, he is the Primordial Chaos Dragon. Who dares come against him?
“So, does this Incubus King work for this Supreme?”
“Yes. His name is King Uny; he was the one who slaughtered my clan and the one I planned on killing one day.
As for the Supreme, she can’t descend to the High Worlds, so I am safe from her. But the moment I reach the Immortal Worlds, she will come for me.”
“Then why don’t you just find a way to destroy this Extreme Pure Yin Body? I am sure a night with a handsome dragon will take care of it.”
Adina looked at Kent with a frown, then she sighed. Kent just laughed.
“It is not that simple. The Extreme Pure Yin Body I have has only partially awakened. If I were to taint it now, it would kill me. So I have to wait until I become an immortal to awaken it fully.
Of course, even if there were a way to taint it before fully awakening it, I wouldn’t. Although it was a curse I never asked for, it has also helped me navigate through the thick and thin.
Without my Extreme Pure Yin Body, I would have long died, so I can’t just do away with it.
I need it, even if it’s a curse that is putting a target on my back everywhere I go. In a way, the Extreme Pure Yin Body is part of me, so discarding it is not an option.

But while my death would probably solve the problem, I now know it isn’t as simple as I expected. Even if I were to die now, my body can still be claimed, and the Extreme Yin Body would fall into their hands.”
“Then, do you have a plan for when it has fully awakened?” Kent asked, but Adina just shook her head.
“I don’t have a plan yet, but I will soon. For now, I want to live long enough to awaken it fully. I will figure the rest out later.”

“Not a bad plan.” Kent chuckled. “If there is any consolation, know that I will get you to your next destination. The rest will depend on your will to live... But seeing you face off against sixteen mercenaries, I am sure you will bitch slap that Supreme when she arrives.”
Adina smiled, hiding her face from Kent; however, the dragon saw it and only smirked.
“Though I have to ask, don’t you have, like, a teleportation device that can take you to this place you want to go? Why come to this place teeming with powerful beasts?”
“I want to disappear for a while, and using the teleportation mountains is the best way. If I use other teleportation gates, they can easily track me.
But with the teleportation monuments, I will be able to have a moment of peace for a while before the danger finds me again. By then, I will know where to go next.”
“Sounds tedious.”
“Very.”

“Don’t worry, I will get you to where you want to go, and if fate wills it, we will meet again. Perhaps then I will be strong enough to go on a killing spree across the Supreme Worlds. Who knows, we might even succeed in killing this Supreme.”
“I look forward to that day.”
Kent then turned to Iver. He studied him with a focused eye, making sure nothing was missed. Soon, he noticed the ring around his finger.
“Dump the contents in your space ring here.”
Iver obeyed and started pouring everything out. There was a pile of spirit stones, which the tower quickly took away and added to Kent’s reserve of spirit stones.

There were also some weapons, some high-level Spirit Crystals, some skill books, and even a technique book for bow users. Iver doesn’t use the bow, but Kent suspected he might have wanted it for someone.
Some armors that Kent had no use for. There was also some junk, including a slab of bone, that Kent ignored at first.
However, after checking everything, he returned to the bone and decided to check it out.
“Strange markings,” Kent studied the bone for a few minutes before turning to Iver.
“What is this?”
“I don’t know. I found it in an ancient tomb, hoping it would fetch me some money, but it turned out to be just junk. I even forgot I still have it in my storage ring.”
“I see.” Kent perhaps expected it to be something good, but it turned out he was wrong.
He squeezed, attempting to shatter it, but to his shock, the bone never broke. “Damn, this bone is hard.”
Kent decided to use his spiritual qi to break it. However, the moment he channeled his energy into it, he felt his energy get sucked into the bone, and then he blacked out, falling on his back.
When he woke up, he was standing within a pool of blood, where the aura of slaughter was both visible and suffocating.
“Hahahahaha....” Suddenly, an evil, laughter-filled with dread, spread across the space.

I found it in an ancient tomb, hoping it would fetch me some money, but it turned out to be just junk.
I even forgot I still have it in my storage ring.”
“I see.” Kent perhaps expected it to be something good, but it turned out he was wrong.
He squeezed, attempting to shatter it, but to his shock, the bone never broke.
“Damn, this bone is hard.”
Kent decided to use his spiritual qi to break it.
However, the moment he channeled his energy into it, he felt his energy get sucked into the bone, and then he blacked out, falling on his back.
When he woke up, he was standing within a pool of blood, where the aura of slaughter was both visible and suffocating.
“Hahahahaha....” Suddenly, an evil, laughter-filled with dread, spread across the space.

chapters.title: Chapter 865: The Slaughter King
paragraphs: "Hahahahaha... Finally, after waiting for so long, you have arrived."

Kent felt a chill run down his back when he heard the laughter. Instinctively, he took a few steps back, but it was futile, for he was standing in a pool of blood with nothing but blood spreading far and wide.
"Who is there?" Kent asked, looking around, his instinct screaming at him to run. However, all he could see was a sea of blood.
There was nowhere to run, and he knew that.
So he was left with one desperate option if it came down to it — to face whatever had pulled him into this godforsaken realm. Kent was ready to battle, and so he prepared himself.
However, when the void cracked red and a large, razor-sharp claw emerged from it, dripping with blood, all hope, no matter how much he felt it, was lost.
The presence that appeared was one he would never have had a counter for. Just gazing at the claw was shattering his mind and pressing down on his soul.
He was outmatched, outclassed, and out of his league, and that realization was all Kent knew to understand that he was in real danger now.
However, he didn’t turn away from the claw.
His gaze was locked on it, and the more he looked, the paler he turned.
A normal person would have looked away, but Kent continued to stare, and for a while, his body started shaking as he broke into a profuse sweat.
His body was screaming at him to look away, but his will as a chaos dragon said otherwise.

"Hahaha... Not bad. Not bad at all. Despite being a mere ant standing before me, you didn’t lose your will to look away but actually kept staring at me. That shows true strength worthy of the last True Primordial."
The claw transformed, and a figure emerged from it, locking gazes with Kent. Kent took a few steps back, but he kept staring.
He was clad in a tattered red cloak, and on his forehead were two long, twisted, red horns. His eyes were red, and his body was covered in golden-red scales that a weapon couldn’t easily penetrate.
"Welcome to my domain, Chaos Dragon," the man said, moving closer. When he was close enough to Kent, two red chairs made from bones appeared.
"Sit."
Kent obeyed and sat down, not taking his eyes off the man.
"You can call me Bhaal’Khar, the Slaughter King." He smiled, but Kent didn’t look amused. If anything, he wanted to tell the man never to smile at anyone ever again.
The smile is evil, and anyone who sees that will break down, their souls extinguished.
"This is the part where you tell me your name," Bhaal said, and Kent felt his body shudder.
"I am Kent, but I guess you already know that. So why am I here?"
Bhaal smirked. "Very simple, actually. You are here to inherit my legacy."
"No, thank you." The feeling he was getting wasn’t one he wanted to experience again, or at least not for a while.
"You don’t have a choice here, Kent. You are the primordial Chaos Dragon, the True Primordial. Without my legacy, you will be stuck at the Core Formation stage forever."
Kent’s eyes widened.

His mind quickly went back to a few weeks ago when he finally reached level 8. Back then, upon reaching the 8th level, he felt like something was missing. Of course, the Tower told him nothing was missing, but Kent could feel it.
This made him start to wonder if he needed a stronger energy source before he could reach the 9th level and form his core.

In the end, he chose to deal with that after he came out of seclusion. Unfortunately, he was pulled into an urgent quest, which left him now on the run against time but also against dangerous opponents.
So, hearing something related to his worry now confirmed, he just couldn’t keep calm.
"What do you mean I will get stuck at the Core Formation stage if I don’t inherit your legacy?" Kent asked, looking more involved in the situation.
In a way, the fear he felt toward Bhaal’Khar was washed away, now replaced with genuine worry.
"Hahahaha... Look at your worried face. Aren’t you the Primordial Chaos Dragon? Why worry over something this small?" Bhaal laughed, making Kent clench his fist.
’This bastard... I would love to punch his face,’ Kent thought inwardly, but it was already too late for him to pull back his thoughts.
He had already been in similar situations and knew whatever he thought would be known by the owner of that realm, so naturally, Bhaal heard his thoughts, causing him to laugh amusedly.
"Looks like you have bigger dreams, Kent. But I guess, as the Primordial Chaos Dragon, you do qualify to punch me in the face.
However, you are just too weak even to pinch me, even if I allowed you to hit my mortal body." Bhaal paused and laughed for five good minutes before returning to the issue at hand.

"I know you are already aware of the True Primordials. I can sense Heliux’s aura on you, meaning you have already come into contact with something that belongs to that Flame Bastard, just like how you have come into contact with two things that belonged to me."
Kent squinted his eyes. "The Claw Art and the Primal Body Tempering Art."
"Bingo," Bhaal said with a cheerful laugh. "You have once used that Tempering Art, but we both know that was in another life, and I wasn’t the one who gave it to you.
But now you have my permission to obtain it. However, the main reason you are here today is because of the Primal Core Formation Diagram.
I have waited for a very long time to hand it to you, and now, after your rebirth, you have reached all the acceptable qualifications to use it."
"And what requirements are those?" Kent asked.
"The 13 Lives and 13 Deaths kind. In short, you can just call it the 13 Rebirths."

Kent swallowed, never expecting there to be something like that hidden within his existence. But he had no reason to argue since he had already seen what Chaos could do after obtaining the Primal Body Tempering Art.
He could only listen to what Bhaal had to say and, if possible, gain a good understanding before making any decisions.
"What is this Primal Core Formation Diagram?"
"Very simple. It is one of the six things you need to be able to transcend beyond the limits of this universe one day. Don’t ask me what is beyond this universe because I don’t know.
However, know that the six True Primordials lived so that the one True Primordial could be born. We did our part, and now we can only give you what is rightfully yours.
On my part, I was meant to pass the Primal Core Formation Diagram, a technique you need to be able to form your core.
You are a beast, Kent, an apex predator, so forming your core like a normal mundane is a waste of your potential.

Of course, there are many methods out there, but the Primal Core Formation Diagram is the best of them all because it is a Primordial Grade technique, and now you will need it if you want to rule this universe one day.
So tell me, Kent, are you ready to inherit the legacy of the Slaughter King and become the King of all Beasts in the wild?"

chapters.title: Chapter 866: The Primal Core Formation Diagram
paragraphs: Kent sat there quietly, looking at Bhaal with eyes that held many questions.
Bhaal could see that, but he was more focused on Kent’s expression than taking the initiative to answer the questions he was already aware of.
Kent took five minutes to compile the questions and decided to ask them all at once.
"First of all, what would I gain from learning the Primal Core Formation Diagram?
Second, wouldn’t learning this new technique conflict with the cultivation technique I am currently using? And lastly, would I become a bloodthirsty maniac like you?"
"Bloodthirsty maniac... Hahahaha," Bhaal laughed sarcastically, making Kent wonder if all powerful people are this annoying.
While he was busy looking for answers, the bastard was having fun, showing no initiative to address his questions.
If he could, he would just smack him silly, making him aware that there is a time for everything.
"Listen to me, Kent. There is no such thing as a bloodthirsty maniac in life. If anything, there are those of us who have seen past the intent to kill and made it ours.
Those you see aimlessly slaughtering people aren’t bloodthirsty; they are just consumed by rage. To know the difference: a bloodthirsty maniac is just an evil term for primal predators.
Those of us who have already transcended the realm of killing understand the difference."
’Tch, you think I will believe something this ridiculous? As the saying goes, once a killer, always a killer,’ Kent said inwardly with a smirk, knowing Bhaal would hear everything he thought.
As expected, Bhaal did hear his thoughts and laughed.

"You wouldn’t understand now, but one day, you will come to understand the true intent behind killing, and when you do, you will know that not all kills hold meaning. You will know when to kill and when to walk away.
You will also come to learn the true meaning behind killing, and lastly, what lies beyond the realm of killing.
So, to answer your question, you need this diagram because it is the only way for you to become your true self.
You are the Primordial Chaos Dragon. You hold the most potent bloodline in the universe, which naturally makes you the strongest.
But with your current body and strength, survival—even in a high world—will be a miracle. So you need a new body, and to that, you must start with the fundamental components.
You are not yet at the stage where you will awaken your Spirit Root, so the first thing for you is the Core. You need a core that aligns with your nature.
As a dragon, you are a beast who stands at the peak of the best race.

You are at the apex, Kent, and so you must claim that primal nature of yours because, believe it or not, your blood makes you a danger, and when people find out—which they will—you will need to represent what you stand for.
You have been through thirteen rebirths and thirteen deaths already, so spiritually, you are already a True Primordial. But strength-wise, you are lacking, so you need a core worthy of your name.
Immortals and gods are supposed to tremble when they stand before you. Your name is supposed to shake the heart of the heavens and cause the Celestials to go to their knees for you.
As for the second question, you don’t have to worry about this new technique conflicting with your true technique.
If there’s one thing I know about us True Primordials, it’s that our cultivation techniques can adapt to whatever technique we learn, making us even stronger.
So instead of worrying, you should be happy, for you will not only be learning a new technique, but it will make your true cultivation technique several times stronger.

Aside from that, it will allow you to learn all the other techniques I have left out there. You already have the Claw Art and the Primal Body Tempering Art. Building your core with this technique will bring you closer to learning them.
Lastly, without forming your core using this method, you wouldn’t be able to learn the other five techniques from the True Primordials waiting for you out there.
And trust me, without them, you will come out as an ordinary person regardless of how strong you have become.
So, Kent, this is your path now, and while you are capable now, know that as a True Primordial, you are not even half your true strength yet."
Kent nodded, not so surprised to hear that.
"Then how does this new method work? The method I planned on using requires a large amount of treasure containing spiritual qi. So, how can I cultivate the new technique?"
"Also very simple. You just have to kill powerful beasts, extract their cores, and absorb them."
Kent nodded again, knowing it was indeed simple. However, he also knew things weren’t going to be as simple as Bhaal made it sound.
"The stronger the beast core you absorb, the more powerful your core will become.
Now, I know you are weak and lacking, so killing Spirit Lords and above might be a challenge. However, I recommend you take on Spirit Lords and above, using their cores to strengthen your own core.
It will even be good if you can kill Heavenly Ascension stage beasts or even Empyreans."
Kent could only look at the madman before him and shake his head.
Inasmuch as he would love to say he has the means to kill Spirit Lords and above, he knew the moment their strength level is above level 5, the battle wouldn’t be an easy one.
Now, to think this madman wanted him to kill Heavenly Ascension stage and perhaps even Empyrean stage beasts, Kent just didn’t know what to say at this point.
He continued to look at Bhaal, who held a smug smile on his face.
"Listen, Kent, the Primal Core Formation Diagram will not only help you become powerful, but it also has many added advantages that you can exploit.
One such benefit is the ability to take on the form of any beast you want. I, for example, am a Panther; however, the Claw Art in your possession shows its true might when a dragon uses it.
I created it while in my dragon form. You are a dragon, so it will come naturally to you.
But there is more, and when you learn this method and form your core, you will know them all. For now, relax and learn it first. Trust me, you will thank me later."
"Fine, I will learn it. But one last question. How many cores do I need to absorb before I can form mine if I were to use the core from Spirit Lord beasts?"
"You will need about ten to form the foundation, which, when compared to the ordinary cultivator, will be a complete formation.
Then you will go ahead and create the Nine Core Gates. That too will need a lot of cores, but you are a True Primordial, so I have high hopes for you.
The Core Gates are just channels that connect to the natural source of energy and help you absorb energy from the universe.
Ordinary cultivators only have seven, and they call it the Seven Refinement Process. But you will go through nine, and each is comparable to a complete refinement of the ordinary folk.

With just one Core Gate, you can be likened to someone who has completely refined their core seven times. This means that after forming nine core gates, your strength will be several times more formidable.
You can ascend to a high world after forming one Core Gate, but before reaching the Immortal stage, you must form all nine Core Gates."
Kent nodded and then asked one last question. Soon, his body moved on the outside, and then he opened his eyes, locking gaze with Adina, who held a worried expression.

chapters.title: Chapter 867: Change of Plans
paragraphs: "Are you alright?" Adina asked, looking at Kent. Their faces were just a few inches apart, so they could each feel the other’s breath on their faces.
"I am fine," Kent replied, feeling a slight headache. "How long was I out for?"
"A day and a half," Adina replied, and Kent jerked up immediately. However, his body was drained of energy, so the moment he stood up, he fell again.
Adina caught him before he could fall. This time, she realized how close they were, so she immediately dropped him and retreated.
"What a baby. We were just having a moment. Why ruin it?" Kent smirked, then he turned to Iver, who was standing not far from him.
"Help me stand up." Iver nodded and approached Kent.
He helped him stand up. Kent smiled and moved out of the tent using the little energy he could muster.
Inside the tent, Adina was panting, feeling her heartbeat much faster than it should.
’That was close,’ she thought, inadvertently reflecting on how close she was to Kent just now. That scared her, for she never expected to come this close to a man.
’I better stay away from him. This brat is a poison.
With that decision set in her mind, she sat in a lotus posture to cultivate.

Kent took out some fruits and started eating, using the energy to strengthen himself. After a couple of minutes, he felt his body gain some power. He turned to Iver and handed some of the fruits to him.
"Eat up. We have a job to do, and I need you ready."
Iver nodded and started eating the fruit. A few seconds into eating, he sat down and began to cultivate his energy.
"Lucky bastard. I initially wanted to use you as bait to capture the Level 8 Spirit Lord Beast here. But now that I need to form my core, I suppose you won’t be dying just yet."
Kent walked back inside and started to make plans for when Iver was done.
Bhaal’khar had given him the Primal Core Formation Diagram, so now he knew how to advance his cultivation base.
However, instead of using spiritual energy from spirit stones or spirit crystals, he would now be using Beast cores.
Though it is not common to use the energy from a beast core for cultivation, only 30% of the energy within it is suitable for cultivating.

The remaining 70% is pure primal killing energy called Blood Energy or Blood Qi. In most cases, demons use at least 5% of this energy to cultivate, with some even using close to 10% to both cultivate and temper their bodies.
Basically, if one had the means, they wouldn’t use beast cores for cultivation, for the Blood Qi inside can easily corrode the body and affect one’s foundation.
However, in Kent’s case, he will be absorbing everything. The idea of cultivating everything was already enough to show just what kind of maniacal path Kent was setting for himself.
He asked Bhaal if he had cultivated the Primal Core Formation Diagram before, and his answer was both yes and no.
According to him, he had only managed to form seven Core Gates, which Kent could stop at if he chose to. He can rise to the Celestial stage with just seven core gates.
However, Bhaal made changes to the technique, which now requires Kent to form all nine before reaching the Immortal stage.
Forming the eighth and ninth was like opening the door to a whole new world of craziness, and while Kent knew all this, he wanted to walk that path, for he could only hope for more strength.
’Bhaal said I will start to see the change after absorbing my first core. I suppose I am looking forward to that.’
Kent smiled and then turned to Adina, who immediately looked away, pretending she wasn’t staring at him.
"I have something to handle up there tomorrow. Do you want to join in?" Kent asked, and Adina looked at him.
"Does it have something to do with me being bait?" Adina asked, and Kent just chuckled.
"No. I just want you to distract it for a moment while I land the killing blow."
"How is that different from being bait?"
Kent grinned, "It is different because you will come out alive in the end."
"So when you first wanted to use me as bait, you accounted for me dying." Adina glared at Kent; a murderous look flashed across her eyes.
"I already told you: until you successfully get to your destination using the Teleportation Mountains, killing you is impossible because I wouldn’t allow it.
That said, I already have a kill move in mind, so the chances of you dying are almost none."
Adina just scoffed and turned away from Kent. After a few seconds, she gave Kent her answer: "I will help you, but should things turn bad, I will abandon you."
"Sounds like someone who has survived on her own for many years. And don’t worry, I wasn’t planning on making things hard for you."
With her added to the plan, Kent knew the first target out of ten, if Bhaal’s estimation was correct, was already in the bag.
The next day, Iver ended his cultivation feeling even more powerful. However, despite becoming powerful, he was still under Kent’s mind control.
While cultivating, Kent used the time to go through Iver’s memories, and what he found out made him change his view on Iver’s character.
It turns out that among the seventeen Red Devil Mercenaries, he was the only one who protested against the idea of taking the mission he was on.
After all, they are mercenaries with a code.
Of course, they had done some dark things in the past, but all the missions he picked were for a good cause.
The last mission was hunting down a rogue formation master who had created a Soul Devour Formation over an entire continent and was using their soul energy to cultivate.

They managed to apprehend him and deliver him to the Mercenary Guild, earning money and praise. It was a big win for them, and even Iver, using the win, proposed to the girl he had had his eye on for a while.

Though he is not the most handsome—no thanks to his rough face tattoos—he managed to win a lady’s heart. But before he could spend time with her, the leader of his group picked up this deadly mission.
He tried to protest, but he wasn’t heard, which ultimately landed them in this hot mess.
It was one of the many reasons he made a run for it when the Bone Dragon was chasing them. But he couldn’t escape because he was attacked by another beast, which now landed him in Kent’s mind game.
So Kent plans to let him go, but first, he wants to use him to the best of his abilities.
Their first mission, though, was to kill the Metal Wing Lightning Hawk.
Its nest is at the peak of the mountain.
The first plan was to catch it and mind control it if possible.
If not, Kent planned on hiring the Tower to help him form a contract between him and the beast by offering as much as he could buy, thanks to having billions in Tower Points.
With its speed, getting to their destination would be fast and less deadly.
But now he plans on killing it and using its core; he will begin forming his Primal Chaos Core, one that he was already looking forward to.

chapters.title: Chapter 868: Soul Universe Unleashed
paragraphs: [The Lightning Peak - Planning]
"So the beast we are going after is a Metal Wing Lightning Hawk," Kent said to Adina and Iver. "It has wings made of metal, making it one of the deadliest beasts you will ever meet.
It is also fast, and yes, it is faster than all of us."
Adina raised her finger, causing Kent to pause and listen to her. "If it is faster than us, how then are we going to kill it?"
She had accepted to join the mission, so it was only right to know that the end of this enterprise would mean the beast was dead and she was walking away alive.
Kent smiled. "It is fast, but as humanoids, we have superior reaction time, or at least we are supposed to have a much faster reaction time.
So that is our play here. I possess a skill that will provide us with a clear view of the battlefield. Now, Iver, since you are the strongest here, you will first make your presence known.
This means you will be the bait. However, you are only required to act once because the moment the beast notices you, it will attack.
You must evade its attack or defend against it.
The moment it attacks, Adina, you will also attack it, doing everything possible to catch its attention at least, then leave the rest to me."

"What if you can’t handle it after I’ve unleashed my attack, and it evades it? Even worse, what if Iver couldn’t evade, or my attack did little to nothing to catch its attention? What then will you do?" Adina asked.
"That is all in my calculation, and I am confident, regardless of what happens, provided it doesn’t attack me first, I will be able to kill it."
Adina wanted to ask more questions, but upon seeing the confident look on Kent’s face, she knew he had high hopes for his plan, so she could only support him.
"Iver, can you handle your task?" Kent asked, and Iver nodded.
"I believe I can take on one attack from it."
"Very well. If it attacks twice, don’t worry; I will be there to handle it. Just be sure to handle the first attack."
Iver nodded, and then the meeting went on for a few seconds before they came to a solid conclusion.
"I trust this team, so we should be able to get this done," Kent smiled, walking out of the tent.
[Master, why do you need them again? I believe with just you, this will be much more efficient, though slightly dangerous. Why do you need them to participate?]
The tower asked, making the smile on Kent’s face deepen.
"Very simple, my dear tower. I need them in the upcoming battles, so I plan on using this mission to gain their trust, and that includes Iver, despite having control over his mind.
As you mentioned, if I go out, I can at most face three Tier 5 Spirit Lords at a time, but I won’t be able to kill them easily.
If I use this mission to show especially Adina the kind of person I am, she will be inclined to accept the crazy plans I have in mind in the upcoming missions."
[I suppose I still have more to learn from the master when it comes to battle and warfare.]
"That you do, tower. Be an obedient assistant, and I will show you the ropes."
After a few minutes, the tent was deactivated, and the mission was a go.
Kent and his team started climbing the 140 km tall mountain.
Iver was leading the way, climbing from one side of the mountain, while Adina and Kent were on a different part.
The moment they crossed the 100 km mark, the peak of the mountain shuddered.
"Soul Map."
Kent immediately activated one of the skills he had awakened from the soul universe. It was a sensing skill that allowed him to see the 200 miles around him.
When he first awakened it, the range started at 20 miles, but now that he was nearing the peak of the Core Formation stage, it had expanded.
"Map Share."
He activated the second ability of the same skill, sharing the map view with both Adina and Iver.
The moment the connection formed with them, their eyes widened, seeing the clear view of the entire mountain appear in their minds.
They saw the beast stir and start looking in their direction.
Iver, who was the closest to its location, was the first person it saw. However, now that Iver had seen everything there was to see about the mountain, he moved, feeling more confident.
The moment he moved, the beast also turned, taking its attention away from Adina and Kent.
Adina then used the moment to get into position. Kent, who saw all this, smiled, knowing his two teammates knew their mission well.
Iver moved swiftly, but he could sense the beast locking its attack on him, so he also prepared his defense.
[The kill strike]
The moment the beast unleashed its attack on Iver, Adina also drew her sword and coated it with a potent white sword aura.
"Looks like she is still hiding her strength," Kent smiled, but he already knew that with the profound sword aura around her sword, the mission wouldn’t be compromised in any way.
The beast, a colossal hawk with metallic wings and talons, opened its beak, forming a ball of lightning. The moment the attack locked on Iver, he felt his hair stand on end.
Kent moved at the very moment because he knew his window had opened.
At the same time, the ball of lightning was fired at Iver, who saw the attack coming, but he wasn’t fast enough to dodge. Even so, she was ready, so he raised five layers of defenses.
BOOM.
The attack landed on the first layer, shattering it instantly. But it didn’t stop there; it shattered both the second and third...

However, when it landed on the fourth, the beast turned to its left and let out a loud screech, but just like Iver, it also wasn’t ready for the white sword arc that came from its left, landing squarely on its wing.
It was sent moving back by the attack.
"Now."
A thin sword oozing with potent soul energy appeared before Kent, and like lightning, it flashed through the air with a hand gesture from Kent.
It zipped really fast, and before the beast could notice what was happening, the sword went through its left eye and came out of the right.
But it didn’t stop there.
Kent used hand gestures again to move the sword at crazy angles, pouring a large amount of soul essence into it.
In a blinding sequence of movements, the sword pierced through the neck of the beast several hundred times in under two seconds, leaving thin golden lights crisscrossing in the air.
When the lights went out, the beast’s head fell off its body and landed on the ground with a heavy thud.
However, before the head even fell, the sword moved and cut apart the lightning ball that was almost on the last defense Iver raised.
If it had managed to reach him, his body would have sustained heavy injuries. However, before the head thudded to the ground, the lightning ball was cut apart, saving Iver.
*Sigh*

chapters.title: Chapter 869: Next Destination
paragraphs: Kent walked close to the headless body of the Metal Wing Lightning Hawk with a smile on his face. Iver and Adina also moved forward, all of them wearing shocked expressions.
They both are powerful Spirit Lords, each possessing great strength and eyesight.
However, no matter how much the two of them wanted to brag, the attack Kent used to kill the beast was one they knew would kill them even faster than it took the beast.
It just didn’t make sense. One second the beast was standing, the next second, its head was on the ground.
And considering Kent was merely a level 8 Core Formation expert, He shouldn’t have this much strength within him.
However, he did, and that scared them.
’I suppose someone whose name appeared on the Sword Dao Tablet is no easy person. But even so, killing a level 8 Spirit Lord that easily just doesn’t seem real.’
Adina said, looking at the smile on Kent’s face as he picked up a head-sized Beast core oozing with energy and stored it in his space ring.
Kent turned to Iver. "Do you happen to know something about weapon refining?"
Iver shook his head.
Kent sighed and then looked at Adina, but she also shook her head.
[Does the master want to refine the metallic feathers of the beast?]
"But of course, Tower. They are powerful soul weapons I can use to cause considerable damage. With weapons this sharp, my dream of killing an immortal might just come to pass quickly."

[In that case, since the master already has a soul flag, why doesn’t the master buy a soul capture skill from the tower store and then use this mission to gather some souls? When the master goes back to the sect, the master can learn how to refine weapons from the elders.]
"That is a smart move, Tower. Let’s do that."
Kent looked at the colossal body of the beast, and his smile spread all over his face. "That is thousands of soul weapons right here."
Kent was so happy, in fact.
He stored away the body of the Beast. However, he saw a look in Iver’s eyes that made him turn to him and speak. "Don’t worry, the next beast will be yours to sell.
This one is too valuable for me to give it to you." Iver nodded, already liking the tone Kent used. ’It looks like I won’t be dying by his hand at least’
Adina walked close to Kent and asked a question, "How were you able to kill the beast so quickly?"
Kent waved his hand, and the sword he had been refining inside his soul universe appeared before him, oozing a rather potent soul energy.
"Wow, that is a powerful soul weapon. How can you have this much soul energy to nourish this sword to this stage? It is just a legendary-grade sword, but it can kill even a Spirit Lord."
Kent chuckled, "If this is already enough to take your breath away, then wait until we meet again a few years from today."
Adina raised her brow. "You make it sound like we have already reached the Teleportation Mountains."
"We will get there soon enough. For now, we have to leave this mountain in four hours and go to our next stop, where we will face another beast.
But until then, I have to leave a care package for our pursuers."
A few minutes later, Kent retrieved the flying boat, and they were already on their way to the next location.
It would take them four days, but judging by the report the tower gave him, one of the teams looking for Adina was closing in on them.

Kent was already prepared to handle them, but he first wanted to absorb the core. With the teams coming, he knew they had to reach their next stop first, where they would have a two-day window for him to absorb the core now in his possession.
[Five hours after Kent and his team left — The Gravedust Brotherhood]
A team of twenty-one Beastmen, each clad in bonelike armor, arrived at Lightning Peak.
"Leader, they went this way," one of them said, pointing at a track left by Kent and his team. Of course, it was all part of Kent’s plan.
"Looks like there are three of them," he spoke again, causing his team to look at the tracks closely.

"How is that possible? We were told there would be only one lady. How come there are three of them?" a blue-faced demon said, sensing that something wasn’t right. However, his teammates just brushed off his question.
"We were told to bring the lady in, and judging by these tracks, there is one lady and two men. This doesn’t change the mission objective, so we should hurry before the others get to them.
Remember, the payday is what we should focus on, not the strangeness of the mission."
"Okay, leader," the blue-faced demon responded and started following his teammates as they began ascending the mountain.
When they were almost at the peak, the tracker stopped. "Something isn’t right."
"What is it?"
"The tracks clearly showed three people started climbing the mountain. However, along the way, one went that way." He pointed to the right, where Iver had gone.
"Now, the lady went to the left."
"They split up. But why would they do something like that?"
"It is simple, everyone. The reason they split up was that they were ambushing something. Now, we should also split up and see if we can find where the tracks went."
The group split into three teams, each with seven members.
A few moments after they started following the three tracks, they all came to a stop in front of three four-foot-tall boxes radiating subtle soul energy.
"What is that?" one asked.
"I can sense soul energy coming from it."
They paused for a moment, scanning it for a few more seconds before they all came to an agreement and moved toward it.
The moment they were three steps from it, they heard a beep sound, making them stop. However, by then, they had already entered Kent’s trap.
The formation hummed to life, and with a smile on his face, several miles away, he snapped his fingers, causing the three boxes to explode in unison.

Regardless of their strength, they were all thrown off the mountain, some dying on the spot, some sustaining grave soul damage, with the only one who managed to block some of the attack being their Level 8 Spirit Lord leader.
The team of twenty-one lost eighteen members. Ten died instantly, with eight dying a few minutes after crashing into the ground 140 km below.
"Two down, nine more to go."
Kent smiled.
If only he had known a day ago, the Green Fang mercenary team met their end at the hands of the Wandering Demon Swordsman.
When they went to check on the explosion he had left for the wandering demon swordsman, they were ambushed and killed within minutes.
This also means the wandering demon swordsman who was supposed to spend five days regenerating his leg now needed three.
Of course, Kent didn’t know this because he never accounted for the ability of the Wandering Demon Swordsman that allows him to absorb the blood of his kills to heal and strengthen himself.
So three days later, the Wandering Demon Swordsman was back on Kent and Adina’s trail, now with extra caution and anger burning in his heart.
Four days later, Kent and his team arrived at the Vine Forest, where his next target, the Vine Lion, is located.
