"But of course, Tower.
They are powerful soul weapons I can use to cause considerable damage.
With weapons this sharp, my dream of killing an immortal might just come to pass quickly."
[In that case, since the master already has a soul flag, why doesn’t the master buy a soul capture skill from the tower store and then use this mission to gather some souls?
When the master goes back to the sect, the master can learn how to refine weapons from the elders.]
"That is a smart move, Tower.
Let’s do that."
Kent looked at the colossal body of the beast, and his smile spread all over his face.
"That is thousands of soul weapons right here."
Kent was so happy, in fact.
He stored away the body of the Beast.
However, he saw a look in Iver’s eyes that made him turn to him and speak.
"Don’t worry, the next beast will be yours to sell.
This one is too valuable for me to give it to you." Iver nodded, already liking the tone Kent used. ’It looks like I won’t be dying by his hand at least’
Adina walked close to Kent and asked a question, "How were you able to kill the beast so quickly?"
Kent waved his hand, and the sword he had been refining inside his soul universe appeared before him, oozing a rather potent soul energy.
"Wow, that is a powerful soul weapon.
How can you have this much soul energy to nourish this sword to this stage?
It is just a legendary-grade sword, but it can kill even a Spirit Lord."
Kent chuckled, "If this is already enough to take your breath away, then wait until we meet again a few years from today."
Adina raised her brow.
"You make it sound like we have already reached the Teleportation Mountains."
"We will get there soon enough.
For now, we have to leave this mountain in four hours and go to our next stop, where we will face another beast.
But until then, I have to leave a care package for our pursuers."
A few minutes later, Kent retrieved the flying boat, and they were already on their way to the next location.
It would take them four days, but judging by the report the tower gave him, one of the teams looking for Adina was closing in on them.
Kent was already prepared to handle them, but he first wanted to absorb the core.
With the teams coming, he knew they had to reach their next stop first, where they would have a two-day window for him to absorb the core now in his possession.
[Five hours after Kent and his team left — The Gravedust Brotherhood]
A team of twenty-one Beastmen, each clad in bonelike armor, arrived at Lightning Peak.
"Leader, they went this way," one of them said, pointing at a track left by Kent and his team.
Of course, it was all part of Kent’s plan.
"Looks like there are three of them," he spoke again, causing his team to look at the tracks closely.
"How is that possible?
We were told there would be only one lady.
How come there are three of them?" a blue-faced demon said, sensing that something wasn’t right.
However, his teammates just brushed off his question.
"We were told to bring the lady in, and judging by these tracks, there is one lady and two men.
This doesn’t change the mission objective, so we should hurry before the others get to them.
Remember, the payday is what we should focus on, not the strangeness of the mission."
"Okay, leader," the blue-faced demon responded and started following his teammates as they began ascending the mountain.
When they were almost at the peak, the tracker stopped.
"Something isn’t right."
"What is it?"
"The tracks clearly showed three people started climbing the mountain.
However, along the way, one went that way." He pointed to the right, where Iver had gone.
"Now, the lady went to the left."
"They split up.
But why would they do something like that?"
"It is simple, everyone.
The reason they split up was that they were ambushing something.
Now, we should also split up and see if we can find where the tracks went."
The group split into three teams, each with seven members.
A few moments after they started following the three tracks, they all came to a stop in front of three four-foot-tall boxes radiating subtle soul energy.
"What is that?" one asked.
"I can sense soul energy coming from it."
They paused for a moment, scanning it for a few more seconds before they all came to an agreement and moved toward it.
The moment they were three steps from it, they heard a beep sound, making them stop.
However, by then, they had already entered Kent’s trap.
The formation hummed to life, and with a smile on his face, several miles away, he snapped his fingers, causing the three boxes to explode in unison.

Regardless of their strength, they were all thrown off the mountain, some dying on the spot, some sustaining grave soul damage, with the only one who managed to block some of the attack being their Level 8 Spirit Lord leader.
The team of twenty-one lost eighteen members.
Ten died instantly, with eight dying a few minutes after crashing into the ground 140 km below.
"Two down, nine more to go."
Kent smiled.
If only he had known a day ago, the Green Fang mercenary team met their end at the hands of the Wandering Demon Swordsman.
When they went to check on the explosion he had left for the wandering demon swordsman, they were ambushed and killed within minutes.
This also means the wandering demon swordsman who was supposed to spend five days regenerating his leg now needed three.
Of course, Kent didn’t know this because he never accounted for the ability of the Wandering Demon Swordsman that allows him to absorb the blood of his kills to heal and strengthen himself.
So three days later, the Wandering Demon Swordsman was back on Kent and Adina’s trail, now with extra caution and anger burning in his heart.
Four days later, Kent and his team arrived at the Vine Forest, where his next target, the Vine Lion, is located.

chapters.title: Chapter 870: Primal Core Formation Diagram, First Core
paragraphs: [200 miles away from the Vine Forest]
"This place looks creepy," Adina said, looking at the coiling and twisting forest 200 miles away from them.
Kent smiled. "It is the Vine Forest, so what do you expect?"
Their next destination was the Vine Forest. However, they weren’t going to stay there. Nobody in their right mind would stay in such a place.
They just want to kill the Vion Lion and be on their way.
Of all the many beasts Kent planned on killing, all were below the Heavenly Ascension stage, for he knew that even using his soul universe, killing a Heavenly Ascension stage beast would not be easy.
Of course, he planned on facing the Wandering Demon Swordsman, who was a Level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage expert.
However, before that, he had planned to form his core and that involved killing Level 8 Spirit Lord beasts. Given that it was within his capabilities, he was determined to do so.
"So what is our next move?" Adina asked, and Kent sat down.

"I will first absorb the core from the beast we killed, then we can go after the next target. It is a Level 8 Spirit Lord stage beast, so we should be able to kill it in mere minutes, perhaps even less if we plan well."
Adina nodded and started to wait for Kent to get started.
Kent took out the core, feeling the bloodthirsty energy pulsing from it. ’This will indeed turn me into a maniac if it doesn’t kill me first.’
He set it down, and then, after taking a deep breath, he formed a hand seal, manifesting a formation diagram.
He turned and looked at Adina. "No matter what, don’t approach me."
Adina, who already wanted to stay as far away from Kent as possible, didn’t need him telling her that. She just moved back further as a sign that she had no plans to help him, no matter what.
Kent smirked and then formed another seal. ’I first have to activate the Primal Core Formation Diagram before the absorption will start.’
Kent formed the third seal, and the formation diagram on the ground started spinning slightly.
A few seconds into the spinning, his cultivation method started merging with the Primal Core Formation diagram.
It took a couple of minutes, but the moment the merging ended, the core before Kent started to get absorbed, reducing in size the next second.
Kent felt his body suddenly fill with so much energy, even when only half of the core was absorbed.
Adina, who was standing back, felt her face pale when she saw Kent absorbing everything from the core. She was tempted to stop him, but she held herself back, recalling Kent’s warning.
’Is he crazy? Why is he absorbing all the energy from the beast’s core?’
She didn’t understand why Kent was doing all this. However, she remained behind, observing as Kent absorbed both the pure and chaotic essence of the beast core.
After two hours, the core was fully absorbed, and Kent fell into a trance-like state.
He appeared inside his soul sea, where there was water everywhere. However, while the water mirrored the blue color of the sky, Kent saw that one part of the water had started turning red.
Of course, he saw that one part of the sky had also turned red.
"The energy coming from the red spot is overwhelming." Kent clenched his fist, feeling the energy seep into his body.
"However, if this core formation thing is measured based on when the entire sea turns red, then I will need more than 10 cores."
This realization made him sigh. But he could also feel his energy rise to a new level, so he knew no matter what, he must form the core before meeting the Heavenly Ascension stage expert.
"There is nothing aside from the water and the 13 moons here," Kent sighed, and then willed himself back to the outside.
When he woke up, a powerful energy burst out of his body, causing Adina and Iver to turn pale in an instant.
"Why do you guys look pale?" Kent asked, not having realized what his aura did to them.
"Your aura is filled with bloodlust," Adina responded, and Kent smiled.
"Looks like it worked." Kent smiled cheerfully.
His smile was one of pure, unfiltered happiness. ’It seems Bhaal didn’t lie to me. Just one core was enough to change something about me.’
Kent activated the ’Soul Map,’ and for a moment, his body froze.
"Are you alright?" Adina, who was paying close attention to Kent, asked when she saw the look on his face.
Kent didn’t answer her immediately.
Instead, he activated the ’Map Share’ with her, causing Adina to stiffen as well..
"How is this possible? And please don’t tell me this is because of the core you absorbed."
"What else could be the reason?" Kent looked at her with an amused expression.
At first, the map could show a 200-mile radius around him, but now he could see 2,000 miles around him, and that alone was more than enough for him and Adina to see the Vine Lion sleeping miles away.
"There is something different about the skill now. I can see some red markings on the beasts body" Adina said, noticing something new inside the Soul Map.
"They are called ’Intent Marks.’ They are the vulnerable spots on a target you can go for during combat. Though not guaranteed to be an easy kill, having this mark makes the battle much easier.
The chances of you landing a fatal blow on these spots are very high."
"Should that even be possible?" Adina was left stunned, unsure of how to describe the Soul Map.
"Nothing is impossible, young lady." Kent laughed, walking closer to the edge of the mountain.
He shared the Soul Map with Iver, who was equally mesmerized.
"As you can see, our next target is sleeping, so this should be easy enough." They nodded. Using the Soul Map, they could see where they would pass without the beast giving them trouble.
The map gave them an overview of the entire 2,000-mile radius, and all they had to do was follow the marked points.
"The same plan as before, so we should get this over with and leave this forest. I plan on reaching the Teleportation Mountains within the next seven days, so we should hurry."
Adina liked the idea because, while she started to enjoy Kents company, she knew the faster they get to the teleportation mountains, the faster she will be on her way to her next safe zone.
They moved, and ten minutes later, Iver came within 50 meters of the Vine Lion, which stirred from its sleep. However, instead of the lion attacking, Iver was the one to attack.
His spear attack was lethal, and while the lion was able to defend against it, the attack that came from Adina landed on its body, cutting a large wound into its skin.
But it didn’t get the chance to go berserk because Kent was ready with his attack.
He unleashed a different sword, driving it through the lion’s brain. It was a single attack, but it was enough to end the lion’s life.
"I might just have a thing for flying weapons," Kent laughed, making the flying sword zip through the air a few more times before returning it to his soul universe.
Adina and Iver could only look at him with unbelieving expressions. They saw enough to know that the moment Kent reached the Spirit Ascension stage, not even a Supreme High World could contain him.
"Let me absorb the core before we leave." He sat down and began to absorb the core.

chapters.title: Chapter 871: Falling Into a Trap
paragraphs: [2 Days Away from the Teleportation Mountain – Bone Cemetery]
"Iver moved back," Kent shouted, unleashing a power sword attack just in time to collide with a piercing bone unleashed by the Bone Dancing Arcane beast.
Adina moved in with a quick attack, one that landed on the body of a colossal bone-type beast. Its bones squeaked but didn’t break.
The bones felt like metal that wouldn’t dent or break.
"Adina, coordinate with Iver. I will find a way to kill it," Kent said before running toward the Bone Dancing Arcane beast.
It had been five days since Kent absorbed the second core. However, after absorbing the second core, he chose to take a break and instead focus more on advancing toward the Teleportation Mountain.
Kent planned to send Adina and Iver away, and then he would get back to the hunt. So they had been on the move for the past five days, and so far, they had killed five beasts.
Kent took the cores and gave the bodies to Iver, who was more than happy with his gains.
However, upon arriving at the Bone Cemetery, a place where only the bones of beasts and humanoids are found, the scene changed.
The beast there was the Bone Dancing Arcane beast, an ancient type of beast made purely of bone. It had great strength.
Kent, who didn’t plan on fighting a level 9 Spirit Lord, saw this as a way to test his strength against a beast of that stage.
He will continue the hunt after his two teammates are gone, so it was the best time to test how much strong he had become.
Of course, he wasn’t using his soul weapons, since it had proven inadequate in this battle considering the beast was practically impenetrable.
The plan was to use the same tactic they used in the past battles to handle this beast, but when they tried, it failed, resulting in this dangerous battle they never planned for.
Kent moved close and unleashed another sword attack.
"Transcendent Heavenly Sword."
Kent formed ten powerful swords and unleashed all ten at the Bone Dancing Arcane beast. However, the beast coiled its bony tail and defended against all ten swords.
Of course, that wasn’t Kent’s main attack. Using the shockwave and the dust in the air, he activated the Flame Wheels skill, giving him a boost in speed.
He zipped across the dusty ground, appearing beneath the bone belly of the Bone Dancing Arcane beast.
’Got your ass,’ Kent said inwardly as he unleashed another attack, this time using pure, unfiltered sword aura to coat his sword.
The dark golden sword aura formed into a sharp arc, cutting clean through the belly of the beast.
Iver used the momentary distraction caused by Kent’s attack to circle the beast and land an attack at where it couldnt easily defend.
Kent was impressed with how Iver’s knowledge of battle seemed to grow every by every battle they fought. He had a way of using the smallest advantage to make the most out of it.
Kent landed another attack taking the attention away from Iver.
Iver seized the chance to unleash a powerful attack at the head of the Bone Dancing Arcane beast.
Its bones squeaked yet again, but Adina was already on the move with Kent, who turned his left arm into a dragon claw.
Adina unleash a sword Arc and Kent Also unleash swung his claw sending red and golden energy arcs at the beast.
Both attacks landed on the Bone Dancing Arcane beast, causing a loud, squeaky scream from it.
Kent moved again, jumped onto the back of the beast, stabbing his sword into the large vertebrae of the creature.
"Iver..."
Kent wasn’t even done when Iver flew into the air and threw his spear like a terrifying javelin, driving a hole through the Bone Dancing Arcane beast’s back.
However, it swung its body, sending Kent flying back, and then it took to the air.
"Shards of Damnation." Kent didn’t allow it to fly away. He activated a skill, driving thousands of shards through its wings.
They all pierced its wings, with a few even scraping the bones.
Kent managed to bring it down.
But that was a mistake he never saw coming.
With the colossal body of the beast, the moment it landed on the ground, a shockwave erupted everywhere, sending all three combatants flying back.
Kent was sent flying toward a large stone. However, before he could slam into the stone, an arrow appeared through it.
"What—"
Kent smirked, forming a hand seal.

Suddenly, the scene in the space started changing. A few seconds later, the colossal body of the Bone Dancing Arcane beast lay dead at the center of the cemetery, with Adina seated on its back, playing a zither.
Around her, a team of nineteen Dark Elves, most holding daggers, could be seen. The strongest among them was a level 8 Spirit Lord. He held a crossbow and was the one thet sneak attacked Kent.
"Looks like you fell for it," Adina said with a smile, putting away the zither.
"What is happening?" the leader of the third strongest mercenary group, the Veilbound Order, who came after Adina, asked.
"You fell into our trap, losers," Iver appeared in the air, holding a white flag with a few dots on it in his firm grip.
The Veilbound Order members recognized him immediately.
"Iver, what are you doing?" the leader of the Veilbound Order asked, but Iver just smirked.
"Don’t act like you are shocked, Domino. This is clearly a trap we set, and you fell for it. Now, keep quiet and die."
"Hahahaha... Iver, do you think you have what it takes to kill us?" one of them said, laughing at Iver like he was the most ridiculous person he had ever seen.
However, he wasn’t done laughing when a chilling tone entered his head, followed by a piercing pain that came from the back of his head and exited through the front.
"He is right, you all should keep quiet and just die."
Kent didn’t know if they heard him or not, but in the blink of an eye, all eighteen members of the Veilbound Order died.
It was a sneak attack, so even the level 8 Spirit Lord didn’t see it coming. Kent appeared from thin air wearing a cloak. He looked at Adina, who sighed in relief and smiled.
"Told you it would work," Kent laughed.
Adina glared at him and then sighed. A small smile appeared on her lips before she sat back on the back of the Bone Dancing Arcane beast.
Acting as a bait wasnt something she wanted, but she had to for the sake of handling a potential danger to her safty.
Kent extended his hand, and the flag flew from Iver and entered his hand. It had more dots on it now, and a few runic arcs started appearing on it.
Kent put it away and removed the cloak he had spent 400 million tower points on just for this ambush. He couldnt use the void yet so he had to use the cloak to hide himself.
A couple of hours ago, they arrived at the Bone Cemetery, where they fought fiercely with the Bone Dancing Arcane beast.
However, they managed to kill it, but not without drawing attention. A team of mercenaries felt the chaos, so they made their way toward them.
With the tower that could actively scan a 50,000-mile radius, they had enough time to lay an ambush, so Kent picked one of the formations Alina gave him and set it up.
Adina’s zither playing was merely a ruse to lower the mercenaries’ guard, allowing Kent to strike when thet never expected it.
Thankfully, with the Veilbound Order recognizing Iver and, not taking him seriously, Kent managed to kill them and steal their souls into his soul flag.
[The master is just 2 days away from the Teleportation Mountain. If the master leaves now, you will reach the Teleportation Mountain before the next team picks up on your trail.]
’That is the plan, tower.’
Kent looked at Adina and then turned back to Iver. ’They have helped me greatly, so I guess sending them away will be the right thing to do.’
After resting for a while, they left, speeding toward the Teleportation Mountains.

Around her, a team of nineteen Dark Elves, most holding daggers, could be seen.
The strongest among them was a level 8 Spirit Lord.
He held a crossbow and was the one thet sneak attacked Kent.
"Looks like you fell for it," Adina said with a smile, putting away the zither.
"What is happening?" the leader of the third strongest mercenary group, the Veilbound Order, who came after Adina, asked.
"You fell into our trap, losers," Iver appeared in the air, holding a white flag with a few dots on it in his firm grip.
The Veilbound Order members recognized him immediately.
"Iver, what are you doing?" the leader of the Veilbound Order asked, but Iver just smirked.
"Don’t act like you are shocked, Domino.
This is clearly a trap we set, and you fell for it.
Now, keep quiet and die."
"Hahahaha...
Iver, do you think you have what it takes to kill us?" one of them said, laughing at Iver like he was the most ridiculous person he had ever seen.
However, he wasn’t done laughing when a chilling tone entered his head, followed by a piercing pain that came from the back of his head and exited through the front.
"He is right, you all should keep quiet and just die."
Kent didn’t know if they heard him or not, but in the blink of an eye, all eighteen members of the Veilbound Order died.
It was a sneak attack, so even the level 8 Spirit Lord didn’t see it coming.
Kent appeared from thin air wearing a cloak.
He looked at Adina, who sighed in relief and smiled.
"Told you it would work," Kent laughed.
Adina glared at him and then sighed.
A small smile appeared on her lips before she sat back on the back of the Bone Dancing Arcane beast.
Acting as a bait wasnt something she wanted, but she had to for the sake of handling a potential danger to her safty.
Kent extended his hand, and the flag flew from Iver and entered his hand.
It had more dots on it now, and a few runic arcs started appearing on it.
Kent put it away and removed the cloak he had spent 400 million tower points on just for this ambush.
He couldnt use the void yet so he had to use the cloak to hide himself.
A couple of hours ago, they arrived at the Bone Cemetery, where they fought fiercely with the Bone Dancing Arcane beast.
However, they managed to kill it, but not without drawing attention.
A team of mercenaries felt the chaos, so they made their way toward them.
With the tower that could actively scan a 50,000-mile radius, they had enough time to lay an ambush, so Kent picked one of the formations Alina gave him and set it up.
Adina’s zither playing was merely a ruse to lower the mercenaries’ guard, allowing Kent to strike when thet never expected it.
Thankfully, with the Veilbound Order recognizing Iver and, not taking him seriously, Kent managed to kill them and steal their souls into his soul flag.
[The master is just 2 days away from the Teleportation Mountain.
If the master leaves now, you will reach the Teleportation Mountain before the next team picks up on your trail.]
’That is the plan, tower.’
Kent looked at Adina and then turned back to Iver. ’They have helped me greatly, so I guess sending them away will be the right thing to do.’
After resting for a while, they left, speeding toward the Teleportation Mountains.

chapters.title: Chapter 872: Till We Meet Again
paragraphs: "So that is the teleportation mountains," Kent said, staring at three tall mountains forming a triangle.
"Yes. The three mountains serve as natural conduits to the universal space channel. It was something created by nature.
Provided you have a channel key that points to where you want to go, you just need to use ten million high-level spirit stones or ten thousand high-level spirit crystals to activate it."
Kent nodded. "In that case, since it was created by nature, it cannot be tampered with, and as such, anyone who uses it cannot be tracked."
Adina nodded.
"I guess nature indeed has its beauties." Kent was rather fascinated by the nature of the teleportation mountains. It was the best way to vanish without a trace.
"In that case, you have to leave now. The next team of mercenaries will probably pick up on our last battle and track us here. The faster you leave this place, the better for all of us."
"Are you tired of me that you couldn’t wait to send me away?" Adina asked with a beautiful pout. Kent chuckled, knowing she was just happy.
However, despite knowing she was just being cute, he couldn’t help teasing her a bit.
"I am afraid if you stay for a day longer, I will be forced to make my move on you, and trust me, I don’t miss."
Iver snorted behind Kent, feeling amused. Kent had long taken the mind control from his mind, but he chose to stay with them before Adina was gone.
Kent even tried sending him away after their last battle a day ago, but he said he wanted to see the mission come to an end.
Of course, the tower was always a step ahead, so it marked him and planted some mechanisms inside his mind for future use and safety. Kent only trusted his legion, his wives, and his dead mom.
Adina glared at Kent and smirked.
"You had your chance days ago, and you blew it," she teased, sticking out her tongue.

Kent laughed, and then he took something from his tower storage and handed it to Adina. "It is a soul-hunting technique called Song of the Fallen. It has a necrotic touch to it, so learning it will perhaps allow you to stay in one place for a while.
I know your main talent is in music and illusions, so perhaps this is the best technique for you. It is a Supreme grade technique, so you probably should pay more attention to it."
Adina’s hands shook, almost dropping the technique scroll in her hand. Hearing the grade of the technique was enough to tell her what she had to know.

Tears fell from her eyes, and while her body kept telling her not to do it, her heart told her otherwise, so she moved and hugged Kent, planting her face in his chest, soaking the poor dragon’s new shirt he bought using 500,000 tower points with her tears.

Of course, as a gentleman, he only patted her on the back. "No need to cry, young lady. It is just a Supreme technique. The next time we meet, I will probably give you a couple of Celestial grade techniques."
Adina stayed in his chest for a few minutes before pulling away with red cheeks.
Kent smiled and then threw a storage pouch to her. "For you not to cry again and soak my shirt, you should open that when you get to your destination."
Adina nodded, still having her red cheeks.
After calming down, she wanted to give Kent something, but she wasn’t sure what to give him. Kent is rich, and she knew that now, so she didn’t know what would be appropriate to give him as a gift.
In the end, she took out her sword and handed it to Kent. "Here you go. I don’t have a supreme grade sword technique, so you can have my sword. I probably won’t be needing it again anyway."
Kent accepted the sword and stored it away.
"In that case, you should be on your way." Adina nodded and flew into the air.
"Till we meet again, Kent," she said, then turned to Iver, "You too."

Both Iver and Kent nodded, watching her fly away. A few seconds later, she was standing at the center of the three mountains. She took out ten thousand high-grade spirit crystals and placed them on the teleportation ground.
The formation activated instantly. Adina looked at Kent again and then, with a smile on her face, she channeled her energy into the Channel Key.
The formation lit up even more, and then, with a beam that separated the clouds, she was transported away.
At that very moment, Kent heard the tower beep, signaling he was done with the quest. He also felt his connection to the Tower space form again.
This brought a smile to his face. He turned to Iver. "Time for you to go too."
Iver nodded. He wouldn’t be using the teleportation mountains because he had a way to get back without the mountain.
He first went down on his knees. "Thank you for sparing my life. In the future, when we meet again, I will be sure to pay back this kindness."
Kent just waved his hand dismissively, telling Iver he shouldn’t worry. He took out a storage pouch and handed it to him.
"Just take good care of yourself. One day I will come to your world, and I will need you to show me around."
Iver nodded, then retrieved a talisman from his space ring. Kent watched him start channeling his energy into it. After a couple of minutes, he was ready to go.
"Till we meet again, Iver."
With a wave, he was also gone.
[Planet Mekyn – The Elven Garden – High Priestess Runa’s POV]
Planet Mekyn is a Great High World ruled by the Elven council.
Their queen, who is also the high priestess of their race, is regarded as the top beauty in all of the Lyall Planetary Alliance and even the Fehime Star system.
She is also a powerhouse and a great warrior who wields the bow like it is an extension of her body.
A while back, she received the Sanctuary request talisman, asking for a sanctuary in her garden where the pure and untainted are allowed entry.
Initially, she was against the idea of taking in a succubus.

However, when she was told the succubus had an Extreme Pure Yin Body, she quickly sent her Channel Key to Adina’s sister, who was the sole reason Adina was still alive and always remained a step ahead of her enemies.
For the past few days, she had been paying attention to the formation platform she had built inside her garden, waiting for Adina with a worried expression.
She would burn kingdoms and shatter planets before she would allow anything to happen to an Extreme Pure Yin Body.
Thankfully, she didn’t have to do anything since, just as her uneasiness was skyrocketing, the formation hummed and a beauty, clad in pure white, appeared.
"You must be Adina. I am High Priestess Runa. I have been waiting for your arrival."
Adina looked around, and all she could see was luxury. However, there was one thing that caught her attention: the priestess smiling back at her.
"You are one of the Seven Virtues," Adina said, fear gripping her.
The High Priestess laughed as she walked toward Adina. "I am indeed one of the Seven Virtues, just like you are one of the Seven Sins.
However, you shouldn’t fear me, for I have no issue with you. After all, we both have something in common."
The priestess unleashed a strand of her aura, causing Adina to calm down instantly.
The priest laughed, "I also have the Extreme Pure Yin Body, and just like you, I am being hunted. However, I believe that with the two of us combined, we can overcome this struggle."

chapters.title: Chapter 873: Time To Hunt
paragraphs: With Adina and Iver gone, Kent was all alone.
He first left the teleportation mountains, knowing full well that the beam of light from Adina’s teleportation would alert all those searching for her.
While he would love to greet them, he knew with his two teammates gone, he had to be cautious, so he first chose to find a safe place.
He used his demi-dragon form, so he was several miles away before the first team that caught sight of the sudden beam from the teleportation arrived.
When he was far enough away, he sat down on a large stone and took out eight cores, each pulsing with energy.
From the Vine Forest to the teleportation mountains, they had killed eight more beasts, making eight cores in total, and he planned on absorbing all before the hunt resumes.
Kent didn’t want to absorb them all back then simply because his primary mission was to send Adina to safety, so he kept them.
Now that he was alone and could do as he wished, he chose to absorb all and see if he would form his core.
He started to absorb the first of the eight cores, already aiming for something good. After an hour, when the first core was fully absorbed, he indeed smiled, feeling some changes happen to his body.
He continued with the second core, and soon, only the last core was left.
Kent was more than happy with the changes happening to him. However, when the last core was absorbed and he still hadn’t formed his core, his mood dampened a bit.

"Looks like Bhaal was wrong in his calculation. I need more than ten beast cores to form my core. However, this isn’t a bad thing. He said the more core I took to form my core, the stronger I would become."
Kent entered his soul space, and truth be told, some portions of the soul sea were still golden in color.
However, the majority of the sea had turned red like blood, and the primal chaos energy emanating from it was filled with the metallic stench of blood.
It was overwhelming, and he could feel it; his strength, speed, and stamina had reached a level he never knew possible just a few days ago.
Now, he knew that if he were to face Spirit Lords below level five, killing them wouldn’t be a problem. He could even tell those below level eight wouldn’t pose a threat to him.
Even if he can’t kill them, he would be able to escape with his life.
The only thing left now was to be able to face more than one Spirit Lord and kill them. That is the dream, and he wasn’t planning on using sneak attacks to accomplish that.

"With my ’Flame Wheels,’ I will be able to run circles around the Spirit Lords. But I still need to form my core just to be sure that my abilities will be enough to kill any spirit lord beast I meet."
Kent exited his soul sea and stood up.
"Though Iver said his world had recently reached the Great High World Level, I can’t underestimate them.
If these were warriors from a Supreme High World, I would have long left this place, but a Great High World — I suppose we will find out who will be running."
"Soul Map."
Kent activated the soul map, and the 15,000 miles around him became clear to him.
His smile spread across his face when he saw it. "They are like fish caught inside a net. I suppose my net has grown wide now."
Looking at the beasts and mercenary teams inside the soul map, he felt like a god. "I can sneak up on them and kill them before they even sense me."

"Iver even said, if I have the means, I should eliminate as many teams as I can. I dont know why he said that, but since I need souls to be able to refine the wings of the lightning hawk, I can only claim these. After all, they came after me first."
With his excuse in motion, Kent planned to kill the three mercenary teams that were within his soul map before getting back to hunting beasts to complete his core.
[First Target: The Iron Vultures]
The first team Kent picked was made up of 26 members, with the strongest being a level 9 Spirit Lord.

The team consisted of orcs, humans, and goblins. The leader of the team was a human with many tribal face tattoos. He held a machete, and judging by the scars on his body, he had been in many battles.
"Kasper, were you able to get any information from your birds?" the leader asked an orc who held a device in his hand, humming a sound.
Close attention would reveal he was listening to the sound of the wind.
Hearing his leader’s question, Kasper shook his head.
"Nothing yet, leader. However, I have my suspicions that the beam of light was the girl we were sent to capture."
"We can’t know for sure, so let’s keep looking for—"
The leader stopped speaking and just stood there, causing his team members to wonder why he had stopped mid-sentence.
However, the next second, he fell back and landed hard on the ground.
"What?" Those close to him rushed to his side; however, when they saw the blood coming from his forehead, they backed away and drew their swords.
"Too late."
Kent spoke as two thin swords zipped through the air with a speed most couldn’t track.
However, even those who managed to track them couldn’t defend against the attack, feeling the sharp swords tear holes in their heads.
Within five seconds, the last of the Iron Vultures mercenaries lay dead on the ground, their souls captured into the soul flag.
"That was easy enough."
[The master only won because he caught them unaware. However, with the master’s cultivation base, he had indeed accomplished a remarkable feat.
But I would like to remind the master that his goal is to kill an immortal before reaching the Spirit Lord stage.]
Kent smiled. "Though the first half of your statement sounded like you weren’t impressed with my achievement, I suppose the last part was enough for me to forgive you."
[The master is the best, as always.]
The tower, of course, decided to make Kent happy.
Kent smiled and then, after performing some minor rituals, he went after the next team using the same tactic on them.
His plan was simple: he would kill the leader first, and when the team became distracted for a fraction of a second, he would attack.
It was a brilliant plan, and it worked well for him. When he faced the second team, he even managed to exchange a few words with them.
However, with the shock they felt when their leader died, they weren’t able to act, allowing Kent to kill them.
With his mental strength currently at an all-time high, he could control a maximum of ten swords without putting too much stress on his mind.
When he was done with the last team, he focused on the beasts.
Forming his core was of utmost importance, so he wanted to get as many cores as he could using both sneak attacks and the power of his soul sea now brimming with energy.

chapters.title: Chapter 874: Primal Chaos Core Formed
paragraphs: "Shit... That was close," Kent said, flying back just in time for the sweeping attack from the wyvern to miss him narrowly.
He moved further back, flapping his dragon wings as he evaded three more attacks from the wyvern, hellbent on avenging its husband.
It had already been 17 days since Adina and Iver left.

Kent, who had been working tirelessly on his core, aiming to form it before leaving the Valley of Torture, was hard at work, doing everything in his power to kill as many Spirit Lord Beasts as he could.
So far, he had killed over twenty of such beasts, with each battle teaching him something new.
With Iver and Adina not there to distract the beasts, not all his sneak attacks worked. However, every failure taught him a valuable lesson, so he kept learning and adapting.
Three days ago, Kent arrived in a region ruled by two wyverns.

When he got there, there was only one of them, so Kent used the same old tactic to kill the wyvern. However, he underestimated the wyvern’s power, forcing him to fight a battle that lasted ten minutes instead of a few seconds.
But in the end, he managed to bring the wyvern down.
Kent took its core and left, only for three days later, out of nowhere, another wyvern started chasing him all over the valley.
At first, Kent thought it was a mere coincidence; however, after using a teleportation talisman he had left in a safe place, he made a quick exit.
However, unsure of how, the wyvern found him.
That was when he realized the reason. The moment he killed the male Wyvern and took its core, while still inside the valley, no matter where he hid, the Wyvern would find him.
"This battle has been going on for too long; I need to end it fast." Kent knew better not to prolong the fight, so the only way out was to kill it.
Kent flew fast past the wyvern, then activated [Fractured Void], raining down a couple thousand sword arcs. This distracted the wyvern for a second.
But that was all Kent needed to use his sword skill, which he had planned on not using for a while now.
His finger trailed across the sword, then, pouring his energy into it, he unleashed a powerful white sword arc.
It streaked across the air and landed on the neck of the wyvern, cutting it off almost instantly. It was as if its defense was nothing before the sword arc.
Kent felt his body drained of all energy as he fell from the air and slammed to the ground with a loud thud.
He panted for breath, taking out Spirit Grape Fruits from his tower storage immediately. He devoured them all in under a minute before he felt his body regain some strength to at least stand.
He moved to the core that had fallen out, then, using his weakened energy, he activated the teleportation talisman he had hidden in the second safe zone he found four days ago.
The moment he appeared in this safe zone, he entered the tower, leaving a marker behind. Two hours later, Kent returned, feeling better now.
"I will never use that skill again until I become a Sword King."
This was the second time using the [One Slash Kill] sword skill. The first time he used it was when he was clearing the fifth level of the Sword Bridge, and back then, he passed out.
Now, thanks to his core almost formed, he was able to withstand it somehow. But even so, he nearly became unconscious.
Kent retrieved 25 cores and put them in front of him.
"Time to form this damn core."
He formed a hand seal and started absorbing the cores like a hungry tiger.
The more he absorbed, the faster it went, so the first core was absorbed within 30 minutes. But he quickly continued with the second, and soon, five cores were absorbed.
When the fifth core was absorbed, Kent felt his soul sea surge. He quickly entered it, and to his shock, the twenty cores left to be absorbed also appeared inside his surging soul sea.
"This looks terrifying," Kent muttered, looking around.
The surging red sea was indeed not a soothing sight. However, he stood in the air watching as it surged for a couple of minutes before a platform rose from the sea.
"The space is expanding," Kent said, flying up higher.
"Bhaal said the initial expansion will determine how much energy I can harness. He said the minimum expansion should be 1,000 km and the maximum should be 50,000 km.
I wonder how far mine will extend." Kent smiled and continued to watch the platform emerge and the soul sea expand.
"1,000 km achieved. Now, let’s see whether I can surpass Bhaal," Kent laughed and continued to watch. Soon, the space expanded to several kilometers and continued to grow.
When it crossed 45,500 km, Kent’s smile bloomed. "In your face, Slaughter King."
He had clearly surpassed Bhaal, so he could at least brag now that the Slaughter King wasn’t there to intimidate him.
However, when the expansion reached 60,000 km but didn’t stop, Kent froze in the air and continued to watch.
"Holy smokes, 220 thousand freaking kilometers." Kent’s mind was blown away by how ridiculous this number was.
It was supposed to be 50,000 km max according to the owner of the technique; however, Kent was now inside a 220,000 km soul sea, and that alone was more than he could ask for.
But it didn’t stop there.
The platform that appeared also expanded by 100,000 km. From the center of the platform, a large orb—or more like a core—made of red and golden colors started forming.
It took several hours, perhaps even a few days, but it eventually formed, reaching a diameter of 25,000 km.
At that very moment, Kent felt his body gain so much power that if he were to fight the wyvern again, he would probably bitch slap it to oblivion.
However, right when the core formed, the twenty cores in the air started to energize Kent’s body. He sat in a lotus posture on the platform, absorbing the energy into his body.

But after a while, he noticed that, instead of making him stronger, it was filling his mind with information on the current stage of his soul sea. It took a couple of hours, but after the fourth core was used up, the process stopped.
Kent took a deep breath, then used his finger to draw a few runes in the air. When the last rune was drawn, three large rings opened from the sides of the platform and started spinning.
Kent wrote a few more runes, and the three large rings reduced in size and then landed in Kent’s hands.

"So this is my Primordial Platform where my power originates from." Kent looked at the two rings in his hands and smiled. "I can even create anything I want from it, provided I have enough energy to sustain it."
Kent let go of the three rings, allowing them to merge back with the Primordial Platform. He formed a hand seal, and this time, the cores moved and started entering the Primal Chaos Core.
"I need to saturate it before leaving." Now that the core was formed and he knew what had to be done next, he left his soul sea and stood up.
"Soul Map."

"Damn, looks like I will be meeting you soon, Mr. Wandering Demon Swordsman." Kent saw the Wandering Demon Swordsman 80,000 km away, showing his soul map had yet again expanded, and this time, by several kilometers.
"Back to the hunt."

chapters.title: Chapter 875: Invitation To The Wandering Demon Swordsman
paragraphs: [The Wandering Demon Swordsman’s POV – 7 Days Ago]
After the blast in the mountain cave several days ago, the wandering Demon swordsman became more cautious as he continued to look for Adina and the person who caused the explosion.
However, whenever he picked up a trail, it led him to an even more devastating explosion or massacre. At first, he ignored it.
However, as he started seeing more of these bizarre sights, his anger began to get the best of him. he felt like he was being mocked.
First, it was just the dead ends he kept encountering.
Then it escalated to the subtle messages he started receiving whenever he appeared at the sites of said massacres.
Eventually, when he began seeing the dead bodies of the beasts, which started about 20 days ago, he knew someone was mocking him, and he wanted blood.
However, everything became worse seven days ago.
Kent killed a certain Panther-type beast after a three-minute battle following the formation of his core. He didn’t use the Soul Universe in the battle, just his sword.
However, when he was done killing the beast, he didn’t leave; instead, he used the beast’s blood to leave a provocative message for the wandering Demon swordsman.
He wrote, "Well, well, well. Looks like the title, The Wandering Demon Swordsman, was all for nothing. The wandering part was on point, for you are indeed wandering aimlessly.
Not only are you clueless, the person you were after had long left this valley, but you foolishly think you have her in your grip.
Let me tell you, Mr. Demon, you missed her by a whole month. So, instead of thinking you have what it takes to catch her and perhaps send her to your employer, here is your wake-up call.
Of course, things wouldn’t have been worse, but all this happened because a mere kid chose to meddle in your business.
You lost to a mere junior, several years younger, several realms weaker.
Now, if you think that was the worst that has ever happened to you, then I want to ask, how did you like my care package I left in the cave? Did it explode in your face, or did it blow your leg off?
By the way, I am still around, so perhaps we might cross paths. Until then, happy limping after me."
The moment he finished reading the message, the body of the beast in front of him exploded, sending him flying backward.
"I will kill you," the Wandering Demon Swordsman said, gritting his teeth as a few burn marks began to heal, dust all over his body.
At that time, Kent was standing 70,000 km away, watching him through the soul map. He laughed and then moved away.
[Six days ago]
The next day, the Wandering Demon Swordsman found another message. This time, he was ready for the explosion even before he read the message.
Naturally, after reading the message, the explosion that never happened was wiped from his mind, replaced by a soul-raging anger.
"I saw how you cursed at me when the beast exploded in your face. Hahaha... I have to say, for a Level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage demon, you sure are weak.
I’ll be sure to spread the word everywhere about how the mighty Wandering Demon Swordsman nearly lost his life to a mere explosion. I have video of both events.
Until we meet again, Mr. Wandering Demon Swordsman. I will keep my eye on you and perhaps leave you more exploding bodies."
With the revelation that he had a video, the Wandering Demon Swordsman abandoned the idea of giving up the hunt and was now more than determined to get his hands on Kent.
He is the Wandering Demon Swordsman, the one every swordsman fears, so they left him alone to continue his wandering.
However, if this video surfaced on Planet Manelaus, he knew people would start looking down on him, and his reputation would suffer a blow.
Of course, with the kind of reputation he has, who would even be stupid enough to look down on him?
[Three days ago]
"I think by now you already know that I have my eyes on you, and so you should be scared. But then I know you want to kill me and sniff my blood, so how about this? Come to the Bone Cemetery.
It is three days away from your current location, and yes, I’ve accounted for your speed. So why don’t we meet there? I already have measures in place for a warm welcome.
There might be a few explosives on the way, so please be careful where you fly through or where you step.
Until we meet, then."
The message received three days ago made the Wandering Demon Swordsman take to the air and start speeding toward the location Kent had left him.
After being humiliated in the past weeks, he had only one thing on his mind: getting his hands on Kent. He wanted to erase the humiliation, so he seized this opportunity to pursue Kent.
[Present Day – Inside Kent’s Soul Sea]
The primal Chaos Core was pulsing with energy as 34 powerful cores hovered over it, channeling energy into it.
Kent stood in the air watching this.
All he could do was wait for the saturation to be over.
Thankfully, by the time the 30th core was absorbed, the Primal Chaos Core gave off a low hum before a powerful burst of energy erupted from Kent’s body.
"Finally," his core was now fully saturated.
Kent didn’t want to exaggerate it, but with his power, Spirit Lords from a Great High world wouldn’t stand a chance. Perhaps those from a Supreme High World pose some threat.
"He will be here in a few hours. I suppose this will be a good fight to see how much I can measure up against a Heavenly Ascension stage warrior."

Though when it comes to knowledge of the path of the sword, Kent was probably at the peak of the Sword King stage; his cultivation base was merely at the Core Formation stage, and his sword energy hadn’t even reached level 6 profound stage compared to the Wandering Demon Swordsman, whose sword energy had already reached its peak.
"He will be out of my league here, but I believe things won’t be too bad if I play my cards right." With his sword skills and Soul Universe, Kent felt like he would do just fine.
Of course, the end justifies the means, and Kent, knowing he was outmatched, had already started making plans.
After an hour, he was ready, so he sat on a tombstone and started waiting for his target.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman was perhaps taken aback when he came to a stop 10 km away, looking at the human seated on the tombstone waiting for him.
At first, he thought he was dreaming, but when he sensed Kent’s cultivation base ten different times, he just couldn’t wrap his mind around the results.
He stood there for ten good minutes, unsure of what to even think. Then he moved, and when he was 1 km away, Kent opened his eyes and smiled at him.
"The philosophy of life is a ridiculous one, don’t you think?" Kent said as he stood up and hovered in the air.
"Here you are, a mighty demon, seven realms above me, but I, a core formation stage youngster, made you come running. Isn’t that ridiculous?"

chapters.title: Chapter 876: Kent vs The Wandering Demon Swordsman (1)
paragraphs: Kent hovered just above the tombstone, looking at the Wandering Demon Swordsman with a smile that contained both teasing and wariness.
He may have formed his core, becoming a terror; however, the person standing before him was still a Heavenly Ascension stage expert, seven whole realms above him.
If that doesn’t call for him to be wary, then there is no telling what kind of maniac Kent had become.
Facing such a demon and appearing fearless was far from normal, and he knew that.
"I contemplated running from you when I first got here, and for a moment I did. I didn’t know who you were back then. However, when I found out who you are, I decided not to run and face you.
However, before the battle, I only have one question, and I would love to have your honest answer. Trust me, it will be in your best interest to tell me the truth."
Perhaps he was still in shock because the Wandering Demon Swordsman just stood there looking at Kent like he was some form of god talking down at him.
Kent didn’t mind the situation because, as it may be, he was indeed looking to have an answer to the question he most surely wanted to ask.
"Is it true that if a swordsman uses their sword realm against those below the Sword King stage, the sword dao will punish them?"
The question was one Kent had forgotten to ask the sword dao when they met.
Of course, Kent already has a partial answer from the perspective of Medium world swordsmen, so he most certainly wanted to get an honest answer from this demon, someone from a High World.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman looked at him for a few seconds before he spoke, "You are from a medium world."
"Any problem with that?"
"No," the Wandering Demon Swordsman extended his hand, and his jagged sword appeared in his firm grip.

"And there is no problem. But to answer your question, know that you are in a High world now, so just die." The Wandering Demon Swordsman moved and unleashed a powerful vertical slash with his jagged sword.
Cling.
The sword landed on a ring, sending the Wandering Demon Swordsman skidding back.
Kent smiled as two more rings appeared around him. The first ring was spinning like a squid in front of him, while one was behind him, and the last was above him.

"Be polite, Mr. Wandering Demon Swordsman. I didn’t send you an invitation because I plan on dying. That said, I have one last question." Kent spoke with a grin; however, the Wandering Demon Swordsman didn’t allow him to ask the question.
He moved and unleashed a horizontal slash; however, just like with the first attack, his sword landed on another ring, sending him skidding back.
He tried again, striking with a powerful diagonal attack, attempting to use the opening between the ring at the top and the one in front of Kent. However, they moved and blocked his sword.
But just before his sword was about to land on the ring, his left leg moved, aiming for Kent’s exposed ribcage.
However, the ring behind Kent moved and blocked the powerful kick, sending him flying back again.
[That was ten percent of his power, master. Be ready, for he is getting angry.]
’I suppose the rings work. It was too draining. But then again, I have four unabsorbed cores powering them, so I can use them for a while.’
[Until the master forms the first Core Gate, he cannot use the rings to channel energy directly from the Primal Chaos Core since that will be too draining.
However, even with four cores active, the master still needs to handle things more actively.]
’I know, Tower,’ Kent smiled, looking at the Wandering Demon Swordsman lock his gaze on the three rings moving around him.
"My question: Is it true you killed a Sword Emperor?"
The Wandering Demon Swordsman looked at Kent with a frown, thinking about how someone from a mere medium world would know something like that.
However, before he could even think of an answer, his body moved, telling him to kill the brat.
He unleashed another powerful swing vertically, but this time, Kent brought his sword to meet it instead of using the ring.
The ground where he stood cracked, revealing the underlying force behind the attack. However, Kent wasn’t concerned about that because he barely felt the force behind the sword attack.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman attacked again, aiming for Kent’s neck, but he ducked and unleashed an attack at the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s leg.
Both attacks missed, but that was just the start of the battle. Though the Wandering Demon swordsman wanted to kill Kent, he still looked down on him, and thus, he wasn’t going all out.
The air crackled with tension as the two faced off fiercely.
They each have their objective in this battle.

Kent wanted to complete one requirement to become a sword sage by cutting off the wandering demon swordsman’s head, while the Wandering Demon Swordsman sought to wipe away his humiliation by cutting Kent’s head off.
In context, they each want the other’s head, though the wandering demon swordsman wants it more than Kent.
The humiliation Kent had put him through was so unbearable that it would have been impossible for him to continue living if it were not erased.
He might even develop a heart devil if he didn’t kill Kent.
So, he was doing everything in his capacity to end the brat, who was finally learning what fighting against the odds looks and feels like.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman’s eyes burned with fury as he crossed swords with Kent. He lunged forward with a furious slash, faster than the eye could follow, aiming for Kent’s neck.
But the brat, thanks to the ’Soul Map,’ was able to see the attack ahead of time.
Kent raised his sword just in time for the two blades to clash with a loud clang.
Sparks flew everywhere. At the same time, something zipped through the air.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman moved back, twisting his body at an unnatural angle as a thin sword grazed his arm, drawing blood.
’Lucky bastard,’ Kent used his left hand to control the flying sword, making it hover behind him.
"Do you like my little trick?" Kent asked with a smile, looking at the Wandering Demon Swordsman, who was a little shocked by the sudden attack he had never seen coming.
"There is more where that came from, so prepare in advance because I expect the battle to be a good one."
The smile on Kent’s face caused the Wandering Demon Swordsman to raise a defense, causing red energy to coat his body.
"That won’t save you, Mr. Wandering Demon Swordsman."
Kent jumped back just as a bony hand burst from the ground and tried to latch onto his leg. Had he been a moment slower, he would have been caught by the hand.
However, Kent wasn’t safe because the moment he landed on the ground, the Wandering Demon Swordsman arrived with an overhead slash.
Boom.
Kent blocked the attack. However, his body was pressed down, causing him to go down on his knees with one leg.
Kent pushed back with all his strength, but the Demon Swordsman was relentless.
He unleashed a mighty kick with his left leg, aiming for Kent’s left shoulder.
Kent smiled evilly just as the leg came. Learning from his battle with his perfect self inside the Perfect Chamber, Kent unleashed three Doom Shards, sending them flying at the leg.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman abandoned his attack and flew back.
’Got your ass.’ Kent muttered coldly.

sentences.text: Kent hovered just above the tombstone, looking at the Wandering Demon Swordsman with a smile that contained both teasing and wariness.
He may have formed his core, becoming a terror; however, the person standing before him was still a Heavenly Ascension stage expert, seven whole realms above him.
If that doesn’t call for him to be wary, then there is no telling what kind of maniac Kent had become.
Facing such a demon and appearing fearless was far from normal, and he knew that.
"I contemplated running from you when I first got here, and for a moment I did.
I didn’t know who you were back then.
However, when I found out who you are, I decided not to run and face you.
However, before the battle, I only have one question, and I would love to have your honest answer.
Trust me, it will be in your best interest to tell me the truth."
Perhaps he was still in shock because the Wandering Demon Swordsman just stood there looking at Kent like he was some form of god talking down at him.
Kent didn’t mind the situation because, as it may be, he was indeed looking to have an answer to the question he most surely wanted to ask.
"Is it true that if a swordsman uses their sword realm against those below the Sword King stage, the sword dao will punish them?"
The question was one Kent had forgotten to ask the sword dao when they met.
Of course, Kent already has a partial answer from the perspective of Medium world swordsmen, so he most certainly wanted to get an honest answer from this demon, someone from a High World.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman looked at him for a few seconds before he spoke, "You are from a medium world."
"Any problem with that?"
"No," the Wandering Demon Swordsman extended his hand, and his jagged sword appeared in his firm grip.
"And there is no problem.
But to answer your question, know that you are in a High world now, so just die." The Wandering Demon Swordsman moved and unleashed a powerful vertical slash with his jagged sword.
Cling.
The sword landed on a ring, sending the Wandering Demon Swordsman skidding back.
Kent smiled as two more rings appeared around him.
The first ring was spinning like a squid in front of him, while one was behind him, and the last was above him.
"Be polite, Mr.
Wandering Demon Swordsman.
I didn’t send you an invitation because I plan on dying.
That said, I have one last question." Kent spoke with a grin; however, the Wandering Demon Swordsman didn’t allow him to ask the question.
He moved and unleashed a horizontal slash; however, just like with the first attack, his sword landed on another ring, sending him skidding back.
He tried again, striking with a powerful diagonal attack, attempting to use the opening between the ring at the top and the one in front of Kent.
However, they moved and blocked his sword.
But just before his sword was about to land on the ring, his left leg moved, aiming for Kent’s exposed ribcage.
However, the ring behind Kent moved and blocked the powerful kick, sending him flying back again.
[That was ten percent of his power, master.
Be ready, for he is getting angry.]
’I suppose the rings work.
It was too draining.
But then again, I have four unabsorbed cores powering them, so I can use them for a while.’
[Until the master forms the first Core Gate, he cannot use the rings to channel energy directly from the Primal Chaos Core since that will be too draining.
However, even with four cores active, the master still needs to handle things more actively.]
’I know, Tower,’ Kent smiled, looking at the Wandering Demon Swordsman lock his gaze on the three rings moving around him.
"My question: Is it true you killed a Sword Emperor?"
The Wandering Demon Swordsman looked at Kent with a frown, thinking about how someone from a mere medium world would know something like that.
However, before he could even think of an answer, his body moved, telling him to kill the brat.
He unleashed another powerful swing vertically, but this time, Kent brought his sword to meet it instead of using the ring.
The ground where he stood cracked, revealing the underlying force behind the attack.
However, Kent wasn’t concerned about that because he barely felt the force behind the sword attack.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman attacked again, aiming for Kent’s neck, but he ducked and unleashed an attack at the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s leg.
Both attacks missed, but that was just the start of the battle.
Though the Wandering Demon swordsman wanted to kill Kent, he still looked down on him, and thus, he wasn’t going all out.
The air crackled with tension as the two faced off fiercely.
They each have their objective in this battle.

Kent wanted to complete one requirement to become a sword sage by cutting off the wandering demon swordsman’s head, while the Wandering Demon Swordsman sought to wipe away his humiliation by cutting Kent’s head off.
In context, they each want the other’s head, though the wandering demon swordsman wants it more than Kent.

chapters.title: Chapter 877: Kent vs The Wandering Demon Swordsman (2)
paragraphs: The moment the Wandering Demon Swordsman abandoned the attack, four cracks appeared around him, and ten doom shards came from each.
BOOM.
The shards landed on the Wandering Demon Swordsman, throwing dust into the air.
However, before the dust could even clear, a powerful red sword arc emerged from the dust, forcing Kent to cross his sword across his chest.
The attack landed on it, and Kent was sent flying away.
"Well, fuck."
Kent moved the rings in front of him, meeting yet another powerful swing from the Wandering Demon Swordsman, who appeared using the power of the Void.
*Qwuark.*
Kent caught blood as the shockwave from the attack landed on his body, slamming him to the ground.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman came for another attack while Kent was still on the ground.
However, before he could get close, two flying swords appeared from both his left and right, forcing him to abandon the attack and retreat.
Kent got back on his feet and spat out blood, smiling at the Wandering Demon Swordsman with his blood-soaked teeth on full display.
"That was close," Kent muttered.
[Indeed, and he is just from a newly Ascended High World. The master must train even more if he wants to dominate the Supreme High worlds.]
"Let’s take it one step at a time, tower. First, I must dominate this bastard."
[I wish the master luck.]

"I need it." Kent laughed, knowing his perfectly coordinated attack met resistance due to the gap in strength. Of course, he felt the attacks from the wandering demon swordsman and knew he was outmatched in both strength and speed.
However, Kent was on the move the next second as the Wandering Demon Swordsman came at him again with even more powerful energy.
His level 9 profound sword energy was also overpowering Kent’s, so naturally, he was out of his league in all aspects. However, Kent wasn’t risking his life going into close combat for nothing.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman unleashed a jab, but that attack didn’t continue as intended.
With a sudden twist, the Wandering Demon Swordsman swung low, aiming for Kent’s legs. Kent leapt back, narrowly avoiding the deadly strike.
The ground shook where the sword had hit. Kent landed and used his leg to throw dust into the face of the Wandering Demon Swordsman; however, he waved his hand, blowing it back at Kent.
’No doubt about it. This demon is good with his sword, but I am better.’
Kent countered quickly. He spun around and slashed toward the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s left side. The blade grazed the demon’s armor, drawing a thin line of sparks.
Kent pulled back his sword and smiled, knowing he wasn’t going to win using basic attacks like this.

As expected, the Wandering Demon Swordsman snarled, seeing the childish attack from Kent. He didn’t care about minor wounds. When it came to healing, his speed was several times higher than that of an ordinary Heavily Ascended stage warrior.
He charged forward again, faster and more furious than before. Kent tightened his grip on his sword, ready to face the next attack.
Suddenly, the Wandering Demon Swordsman vanished in a blur. Before Kent could react, the demon appeared behind him, swinging his jagged sword.
Kent rolled forward, barely escaping the blow. He jumped to his feet and shouted, "You’ll have to do better than that!"
The swordsman growled and charged with a roar. The battle raged on, Kent doing his best to remain alive long enough to learn every last move the Wandering Demon Swordsman was making.
Forty-five minutes later, a smile appeared on Kent’s face, and the Wandering Demon Swordsman sensed something was wrong.
However, Kent didn’t allow him to figure it out as he lunged at him and unleashed a furious swing. The moment he had been waiting for had arrived, and so he wasn’t planning on letting the demon know.

Kent aimed for his neck, but the Wandering Demon Swordsman evaded and swung his sword upward, but this time Kent merely sidestepped and kicked hard, landing his foot on the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s chest.
He was pushed back by the kick, but he twisted his body and dodged a thick shard that shot at him from the ground.
’Ah, the twist,’ Kent smiled, kicking his foot again. This time, he heard a crackling sound come from the side of the Wandering Demon Swordsman, showing the kick did its job.

The Wandering Demon Swordsman caught blood, but he wasn’t in a condition to focus on that, since before he could even recover from the broken ribs, Kent unleashed two sword arcs, landing on his chest.
"You may be a Sword King, but when it comes to using the sword, I am better than you."
Kent said as he activated the Flame Wheel and closed in on the Wandering Demon Swordsman, landing three more attacks.
Two were defended against, but the last landed on his shoulder, cutting a rather deep wound on the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s shoulder. However, the wound healed much faster than Kent expected.
’His healing ability is good, but I now know all his moves, so I can cut him more. That will wear him out.’ Kent smiled as he unleashed another attack.
However, before the sword arc could reach the Wandering Demon Swordsman, he activated his sword realm, changing the scene of the battle.
Kent appeared inside a space filled with the scent of blood. His body immediately felt weaker, as if all his energy had drained away. But that was jsut the initial changes.
The complete change soon came to life, revealing the slaughter realm that the Wandering Demon Swordsman had comprehended as his sword realm.
"You asked whether a sword realm can be used against someone below the Sword King stage. Here is your answer," the Wandering Demon Swordsman said, pointing his sword at Kent, "Now, prepare to die."
"Blood Howling Strike," he unleashed a powerful attack, sending a red blood arc, one that howled with the wind as it approached Kent.
It contained his intent and realm influence, making it several times dangerous.
If the attack were unleashed outside, it wouldn’t have that much firepower. But inside the Sword Realm, the Wandering Demon Swordsman had some form of influence over his attacks.

However, as much as the Wandering Demon Swordsman would have loved to see his attack cleave through Kent’s body, just like it should. When the sword was mere inches from Kent, an evil smile appeared on his face, and then he snapped his fingers.
The sword arc vanished along with the Sword Realm. Both Kent and the Wandering Demon Swordsman were back outside.
Kent held a smile on his face while the Wandering Demon Swordsman showed both shock and fear.
"How?" he asked, but Kent just smiled at him.
"Wouldn’t you want to know my big secret? I won’t tell you, but I have to say, for a peak Sword King, your sword realm is rather terrible.
Makes me wonder if you really put a lot of thought into it, or if you merely conceptualized the slaughter realm like it was the coolest thing to do.
I am disappointed, and for that, I will show you what real swordsmanship looks like.
’Clone Bodies.’"
Three clone bodies appeared, each looking exactly like Kent.
Kent’s eyes turned golden red, showing he had activated one percent of his bloodline.
"Here I come." The three clone bodies activated Flame Wheels and moved simultaneously with Kent.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman, seeing something new, was lost on what to do.
His mind spun, looking for the real Kent. However, before he could figure it out, Kent appeared before him, unleashing a powerful swing.
