chapters.title: Chapter 878: Kent vs The Wandering Demon Swordsman (3)
paragraphs: "Void Cleave"
Kent appeared to the left of the Wandering Demon Swordsman and unleashed the Void Cleave attack, sending a powerful sword arc out.
"Rapid Slash"
He appeared on his right again and unleashed a rapid sword slash, sending 450 sword arcs at the Wandering Demon Swordsman. But it didn’t stop there.
"Transcendent Heavenly Sword"
Ten swords appeared in the air and merged, forming one large sword that shot straight at the Wandering Demon Swordsman.
"Dragon Sword Strike"
Kent unleashed the fourth strike, manifesting a large flame dragon coated in sword aura.
All four attacks arrived at the same time.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman was snapped out of the shocked state he was caught in when Kent unleashed his Clone bodies.
He unleashed a powerful wave of sword intent and sword aura.
However, aside from cutting a few sword arcs from the Rapid Slash unleashed by Kent, the rest landed on his body, sending him flying back. Kent didn’t give him a moment of rest.
Two of his clone bodies jumped into the air.
Kent swapped places with the first clone and unleashed another Void Cleave, then he swapped with the second and unleashed ’Limitless Sword Arcs.’
The third clone body unleashed Rapid Slash again.
The attacks overwhelmed the Wandering Demon Swordsman, but Kent knew it was nowhere close to dying, so he intensified his assaults.
"You can’t kill what is not real." The Wandering Demon Swordsman chopped off the head of one of the clones; however, the next second, another one appeared.
Kent laughed and then swapped with the next clone just in time for the sword of the Wandering Demon Swordsman to pierce the chest of the clone he swapped with.
If he were a moment slower, the attack would have landed on his main body.
However, it didn’t stop there. The moment the clone died, two more appeared.
This made the Wandering Demon Swordsman hesitate, unsure which one to attack. But before he could decide, a lightning bolt came from another clone Kent had swapped places with.
It landed on his body, burning the armor.
"Looks like my lightning grew stronger after forming a core."
Kent swapped with another clone and used his hand to control three swords, each aimed at different parts of the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s body.
He managed to defend against all three, but a stabbing attack from the closest clone sent him flying back. Kent pressed on, not allowing the moment to pass by.
With the ’Soul Map,’ Kent was going for all the Intent Marks he could see on the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s body. They were like calling cards, calling him to strike those spots.
Kent wasted none of these marks since he knew, for now, the Wandering Demon Swordsman had nothing new to show him when it came to the path of the sword.
The only advantage he had as a Sword King was his ’Sword Realm.’ But since Kent rendered it useless for the next 24 hours using the Rule Breaker skill, he was back to nothing.
Kent was very good with his sword, and with his cheat-like Soul Map, he was having a field day with the Wandering Demon Swordsman.
’He may be faster and stronger than I, but I know all his moves before he makes them. Now, I just have to find a way to kill him.’
Kent already had a way to kill the Wandering Demon Swordsman; however, he wasn’t sure using it was the right thing to do.
He had already used the ’One Slash Kill’ twice, and the results were him passing out the first time and losing all his strength the second time.
So he wasn’t banking on it to win this battle.
In the event that his attack didn’t kill the bastard, he would become drained, or he might even pass out, meaning his life was over, thanks to his own skill.
So Kent wasn’t planning on using that.
He could only do his best to find another way.
’I need more clones.’

Kent said inwardly before ten clones appeared and spread out on the battlefield. They each emitted a faint killing intent. The moment the Wandering Demon Swordsman felt this, his instinct told him to run.
And he tried to run. However, Kent unleashed a flame attack that manifested a bone skull in the air. The skull slammed into his body, sending him flying down.
"Running is not an option, Mr." Kent laughed because he knew this battle was his now, and he knew what must be done to kill the bastard.
[The Wandering Demon Swordsman POV]
From the start of the battle, the Wandering Demon Swordsman was having a field day with Kent. He had the upper hand, and no matter how hard Kent tried, his attacks kept pushing him back.
However, with the three rings around Kent’s body, most of his attacks were being blocked. Of course, as a Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator, he could sense it; the rings were draining Kent.
This gave him the idea to pressure Kent more. However, what he didn’t know was that the rings were merely eating away at the four Level 8 Spirit Lord Cores and not from Kent’s own core.

Kent was merely using an external energy source to power the rings, forcing him to reveal his sword moves and battle style. Since he didn’t know Kent was doing something like that, he was eager to wear away Kent’s energy.
Slowly, he started to see that the openings in Kent’s defense began to close.

First, it was his exposed neck. While he was at first pushing Kent to the corner with all attacks aimed at his neck, this time Kent used the rings to actively block him before he even had the chance to attack.
Then came his legs, shoulders, chest, and chest.
Slowly, Kent’s defenses were sealed.
That was when he saw the need to activate his Sword Realm.

However, the victory he was aiming for didn’t happen. Just when he was confident his most powerful attack would take care of Kent, the boy just snapped his fingers, and he lost access to his Sword Realm.
Then his nightmare began.
"He has clones." The moment the clones appeared, and each started attacking, he knew he had to run.
However, he learned a long time ago that extensive use of clones tends to slow down a person. So he was holding on, aiming for when Kent would become tired.
However, he was shocked when an hour later, Kent kept going, and instead of Kent getting tired, he was the one becoming sluggish.
Then it happened.

"Ten clones. Just who is this kid? Is he perhaps a big shot from a Supreme High world who has suppressed his cultivation base just to mess with me?" The thought flashed through his mind, and like gaining enlightenment, he chose to run.
It was better to keep his life than his reputation. If he lived, he could hunt down Kent and end him for good.
However, Kent didn’t allow him to run. He spread out his clone bodies, putting them at points the Wandering Demon Swordsman could use to escape.
"Flame that ignites the heart, burns the soul, and turns the body to ash. Heed my call and grant me thy power." Kent distanced himself and then spoke the last incantation.
"Flame Lord’s Dominion."

A flame tattoo appeared on Kent’s forehead, and the sword in his hand ignited. Kent raised it over his head and then took one significant slash, sending a powerful sword arc at the Wandering Demon Swordsman.

The wandering demon swordsman swung his sword, sending a powerful sword arc at the approaching flame arc. The two attacks met, and a powerful explosion that blinded both Kent and the Wandering Demon Swordsman erupted.
"Death is the only way."
Kent waved his hand, and ten flaming swords appeared behind him. With a wave of his hand, they moved.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman didn’t see them come, but like hot, piercing needles, the swords went through his chest 340 times in under five seconds, leaving a gaping hole in his chest.

sentences.text: "Void Cleave"
Kent appeared to the left of the Wandering Demon Swordsman and unleashed the Void Cleave attack, sending a powerful sword arc out.
"Rapid Slash"
He appeared on his right again and unleashed a rapid sword slash, sending 450 sword arcs at the Wandering Demon Swordsman.
But it didn’t stop there.
"Transcendent Heavenly Sword"
Ten swords appeared in the air and merged, forming one large sword that shot straight at the Wandering Demon Swordsman.
"Dragon Sword Strike"
Kent unleashed the fourth strike, manifesting a large flame dragon coated in sword aura.
All four attacks arrived at the same time.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman was snapped out of the shocked state he was caught in when Kent unleashed his Clone bodies.
He unleashed a powerful wave of sword intent and sword aura.
However, aside from cutting a few sword arcs from the Rapid Slash unleashed by Kent, the rest landed on his body, sending him flying back.
Kent didn’t give him a moment of rest.
Two of his clone bodies jumped into the air.
Kent swapped places with the first clone and unleashed another Void Cleave, then he swapped with the second and unleashed ’Limitless Sword Arcs.’
The third clone body unleashed Rapid Slash again.
The attacks overwhelmed the Wandering Demon Swordsman, but Kent knew it was nowhere close to dying, so he intensified his assaults.
"You can’t kill what is not real." The Wandering Demon Swordsman chopped off the head of one of the clones; however, the next second, another one appeared.
Kent laughed and then swapped with the next clone just in time for the sword of the Wandering Demon Swordsman to pierce the chest of the clone he swapped with.
If he were a moment slower, the attack would have landed on his main body.
However, it didn’t stop there.
The moment the clone died, two more appeared.
This made the Wandering Demon Swordsman hesitate, unsure which one to attack.
But before he could decide, a lightning bolt came from another clone Kent had swapped places with.
It landed on his body, burning the armor.
"Looks like my lightning grew stronger after forming a core."
Kent swapped with another clone and used his hand to control three swords, each aimed at different parts of the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s body.
He managed to defend against all three, but a stabbing attack from the closest clone sent him flying back.
Kent pressed on, not allowing the moment to pass by.
With the ’Soul Map,’ Kent was going for all the Intent Marks he could see on the Wandering Demon Swordsman’s body.
They were like calling cards, calling him to strike those spots.
Kent wasted none of these marks since he knew, for now, the Wandering Demon Swordsman had nothing new to show him when it came to the path of the sword.
The only advantage he had as a Sword King was his ’Sword Realm.’ But since Kent rendered it useless for the next 24 hours using the Rule Breaker skill, he was back to nothing.
Kent was very good with his sword, and with his cheat-like Soul Map, he was having a field day with the Wandering Demon Swordsman.
’He may be faster and stronger than I, but I know all his moves before he makes them.
Now, I just have to find a way to kill him.’
Kent already had a way to kill the Wandering Demon Swordsman; however, he wasn’t sure using it was the right thing to do.
He had already used the ’One Slash Kill’ twice, and the results were him passing out the first time and losing all his strength the second time.
So he wasn’t banking on it to win this battle.
In the event that his attack didn’t kill the bastard, he would become drained, or he might even pass out, meaning his life was over, thanks to his own skill.
So Kent wasn’t planning on using that.
He could only do his best to find another way.
’I need more clones.’
Kent said inwardly before ten clones appeared and spread out on the battlefield.
They each emitted a faint killing intent.
The moment the Wandering Demon Swordsman felt this, his instinct told him to run.
And he tried to run.
However, Kent unleashed a flame attack that manifested a bone skull in the air.
The skull slammed into his body, sending him flying down.
"Running is not an option, Mr." Kent laughed because he knew this battle was his now, and he knew what must be done to kill the bastard.
[The Wandering Demon Swordsman POV]
From the start of the battle, the Wandering Demon Swordsman was having a field day with Kent.
He had the upper hand, and no matter how hard Kent tried, his attacks kept pushing him back.
However, with the three rings around Kent’s body, most of his attacks were being blocked.
Of course, as a Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator, he could sense it; the rings were draining Kent.
This gave him the idea to pressure Kent more.
However, what he didn’t know was that the rings were merely eating away at the four Level 8 Spirit Lord Cores and not from Kent’s own core.
Kent was merely using an external energy source to power the rings, forcing him to reveal his sword moves and battle style.
Since he didn’t know Kent was doing something like that, he was eager to wear away Kent’s energy.
Slowly, he started to see that the openings in Kent’s defense began to close.
First, it was his exposed neck.
While he was at first pushing Kent to the corner with all attacks aimed at his neck, this time Kent used the rings to actively block him before he even had the chance to attack.
Then came his legs, shoulders, chest, and chest.
Slowly, Kent’s defenses were sealed.
That was when he saw the need to activate his Sword Realm.
However, the victory he was aiming for didn’t happen.
Just when he was confident his most powerful attack would take care of Kent, the boy just snapped his fingers, and he lost access to his Sword Realm.
Then his nightmare began.
"He has clones." The moment the clones appeared, and each started attacking, he knew he had to run.
However, he learned a long time ago that extensive use of clones tends to slow down a person.
So he was holding on, aiming for when Kent would become tired.
However, he was shocked when an hour later, Kent kept going, and instead of Kent getting tired, he was the one becoming sluggish.
Then it happened.
"Ten clones.
Just who is this kid?

Is he perhaps a big shot from a Supreme High world who has suppressed his cultivation base just to mess with me?" The thought flashed through his mind, and like gaining enlightenment, he chose to run.
It was better to keep his life than his reputation.
If he lived, he could hunt down Kent and end him for good.
However, Kent didn’t allow him to run.
He spread out his clone bodies, putting them at points the Wandering Demon Swordsman could use to escape.
"Flame that ignites the heart, burns the soul, and turns the body to ash.
Heed my call and grant me thy power." Kent distanced himself and then spoke the last incantation.
"Flame Lord’s Dominion."
A flame tattoo appeared on Kent’s forehead, and the sword in his hand ignited.
Kent raised it over his head and then took one significant slash, sending a powerful sword arc at the Wandering Demon Swordsman.
The wandering demon swordsman swung his sword, sending a powerful sword arc at the approaching flame arc.
The two attacks met, and a powerful explosion that blinded both Kent and the Wandering Demon Swordsman erupted.
"Death is the only way."
Kent waved his hand, and ten flaming swords appeared behind him.
With a wave of his hand, they moved.
The Wandering Demon Swordsman didn’t see them come, but like hot, piercing needles, the swords went through his chest 340 times in under five seconds, leaving a gaping hole in his chest.

chapters.title: Chapter 879: You can call me Kent Madson
paragraphs: "Haa."
Kent sighed, putting away the flying swords.
"I am still weak."
Despite just killing someone seven realms above him, he still felt weak.
"Tower, I want you to measure my performance against an opponent from a Supreme High World. Then tell me the percentage that I will die fighting them."
[The master in his current form, factoring in the Primal Chaos Core but not his bloodline, would have an 8% chance of killing a Level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage from a Supreme High World.

If the master were to use his bloodline at 3%, he would have a 38% chance of killing the same person. However, if the master were to raise the mastery level of his skills to perfection, then his chances of success, everything included, will rise to 54%.]
Kent smiled slightly, unsure if he had to look down on himself or be proud. Thankfully, the tower knew when to come into play.

[But the master should know that he still hasn’t refined his core yet. According to the information I have, the master must form one of the nine Core gates before the master can be regarded as someone who has refined their core seven times.
That said, if the master had formed his core before this battle, things would have ended much faster and less taxing. Also, there is the part about the master’s sword path.
So I suppose I should say the current form of the master is ready for a Great High world, but can’t dominate it yet.]
"So in the end, I am still not strong enough to dominate even a Great High World."

[Yes. The master in his current form can easily face multiple Spirit Sovereigns and walk out unscathed. However, without sneaking up on the Spirit Lords, you aren’t within your current capacity to dominate a Great High world. However, there is a light to this.]
"I sure would want to know, Tower."
[The master only used 1% of his bloodline powers despite having access to 3%. If the master were to use all 3%, then even Spirit Lords, provided they don’t number in hundreds, can be handled.

Also, if the master were to raise his sword mastery to Sword Sage, things would go more easily for him next time. But for now, the master shouldn’t antagonize any Heavenly Ascension stage expert. They are not simple at all.
The one you killed wasn’t truly a worthy Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator or a proper Sword King, and I think you know it.]
"Yeah," Kent smiled weakly, "Stealing power from the blood of his kills through a forbidden art does have its downsides."
[Indeed. So the master should be careful when around Heavenly Ascension stage experts for now, until perhaps the master has formed his core gate and managed to learn the Primal Body Tempering Art.]
"Good to know. But now that this bastard is dead, I suppose it is time for me to leave," Kent sighed and was about to turn around when the tower spoke again.

[The master must cut his head off and send it to the Olive Sword Guild. It is on Planet Menelaus, where Iver is from. Before the requirement is marked as completed, you must send it to the designated location.
Killing him is but the first part of the requirement.
Thankfully, I have the coordinates to that world so you can go there using the ’World Teleporter.’]
"In that case," Kent’s sword moved swiftly, and the head of the wandering demon swordsman came off, "it’s time for me to hit the road. I will return here soon to continue to hunt."
Kent put away the head and his sword and activated the World Teleporter. Soon, he was gone from the Valley of Torture.
[Planet Mekyn – The Elven Garden – Adina and the High Priestess]
It had already been a month since Adina arrived on Planet Mekyn. As a ’Great’ High World, she was surrounded by powerful cultivators.
Even the High Priestess was a Level 3 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator. Since she also possessed the Extreme Pure Yin Body, Adina felt at peace knowing she was no longer alone in her endeavors.
She learned that, despite the High Priestess having the same body constitution as her, she wasn’t on the run. This was because of the Planet Protector.
According to the priestess, the Planet Protector was a heavenly genius, one who appeared once every million years.
Thanks to her protection, she has been able to remain in her world for thousands of years. Though not the strongest world in their planetary alliance, she was protected by someone very powerful.

Adina wanted to meet this Planet Protector, but the High Priestess told her she was in seclusion. However, she was still aware of her presence. This made Adina feel at home, so from the moment she arrived, she started to live a good life.
Of course, at first, she wanted to open the pouch Kent gave her, but she couldn’t bring herself to open it for fear she would find something she couldn’t handle.
And so weeks passed, and finally, she managed to gather the courage to open the pouch.
What she found inside took her breath away, just as Kent had planned.
There were many heaviness-defying fruits inside the pouch, billions of spirit stones, and, well, thousands of cultivation resources, including some armors and quick getaway treasures.
Then spent half his fortune in Tower Points to make sure she was sent away with enough to keep her alive for the time being.
Adina was indeed shocked to find all these treasures. However, what shocked her the most was the two scrolls inside the pouch.
One was addressed to her and the other to the High Priestess, whom Kent named ’Adina’s guardian.’
Adina contemplated reading it first, but in the end, she went and handed it over to the High Priestess, who quickly opened it and began to read.
"I know you don’t know me, and I also don’t know you. However, know that when it comes to Adina, I am her guardian, so please take care of her.
I planned to come get her one of these days, but before then, you must make sure she takes her cultivation seriously and, should the need call for it, make sure she runs as far away as possible.

I don’t know what martial technique will be suitable for you, so I’ve added a God Grade cloning technique in this scroll instead. Learn it and use it to protect her. I will reward you when we meet in person.
And oh, one last thing... You can call me Kent Madson."
When the High Priestess was done reading the scroll, her jaw was almost on the ground. Adina, who didn’t know what had happened, walked behind her and chose to see what was written in the letter.
When she saw the message, she was equally mesmerized and even blushed thanks to Kent’s shamelessness.
She had yet to read her scroll, but seeing what Kent wrote in the letter addressed to the Priestess, she knew her own would leave her wishing she had never met Kent.
Even so, she looked forward to her own.
"Are you alright, Big Sister?" Adina asked. She and the High Priestess had become sworn sisters, so she addressed her as such.
The High Priestess turned and looked at her for a few seconds before speaking two words.
"Let’s go."
The priestess didn’t say where they were going, but Adina followed her. They flew away from the garden and headed toward a small house sitting atop a mountain where only white plants grew.
The moment they approached the house, Adina felt her body enveloped by a superior energy, one that could seize her body at any moment.
And the worst part, she knew no matter what she did, she wouldn’t be able to free herself.
They landed on soft white grass and walked forward for a few seconds before the High Priestess, who was also the Queen, went down on her knees. Adina followed her promptly.
"Great Planet Guardian, we want to have an audience with you... It is about Kent Madson."
The door opened the next second, and their bodies were dragged inside. It closed promptly...

chapters.title: Chapter 880: Lady Enyo
paragraphs: While Adina was looking forward to meeting a mysterious, perhaps ancient, old lady, the face that greeted him was that of a beauty, not even a year older than the High Priestess.
She had purple hair that fell down her back and a pair of golden eyes. She was, in fact, a beauty who would make many men drool at the sight of her.
The aura around her was also calm and welcoming, almost harmless if one doesn’t know what she is and what she has done with her Bow and Arrow.
They appeared before her like ghosts, and the first question she asked was, of course, about the one called Kent Madson.
"What do you know about Kent Madson?" The question was directed at Adina.
She gulped, feeling the overwhelming aura, though a welcoming one, swirl around the lady.
"I met him on my way to this world. He was the one who saved me and ensured I reached the teleportation mountains in one piece."

The lady sighed in her heart, knowing her window had closed. It had been a month since Adina arrived in Mekyn, so she knew Kent would be long gone by now. If she were to go there, she would be too late.
But even so, she wanted to know more about him.
To the rest of the universe, Kent Madson became popular a few months ago, but to Lady Enyo, Kent Madson had been appearing in her dreams for three good years now.
She started dreaming about him at about the same time Kent arrived in Sonox.

At first, it was just flashes of dreams of this boy whose smile was brighter than stars. Back then, she would occasionally wake up smiling. It even made her want to go to sleep every evening so that she could dream about him.
However, as months passed, the dreams started demanding answers.
It got to the point she had to drop everything and focus on finding everything she could about this mysterious Kent Madson. However, no matter how hard she looked, she found nothing.
It made her pull away from the outside and seclude herself in her small mountain abode.
However, a few months ago, rumors began spreading about a mysterious name that suddenly appeared on the Sword Dao tablet.
The Kent Madson that made her think she was going mad became known to everyone, and just like what happened to her, everyone started looking for him.
The name was known to many, but there was no face to the name. At first, many youngsters tried to use the name to gain the favour of immortals, but they regretted it in mere hours.
And so for weeks now, nobody dares come out claiming to be Kent Madson.
The name Kent Madson was a mystery.
She tried her best, but knowing it was never going to pan out in the end, she entered a state of self-imposed seclusion, telling everyone not to disturb her.
But now, she was more eager to learn more about Kent Madson from someone who actually saw him.
"What was he like?" Lady Enyo asked.
Adina smiled, "Shameless. That is the best way I can describe him. That shameless bastard."

For some strange reason, Lady Enyo smiled, recalling some moment in her dream where this Kent Madson would beat his chest and brag about something he could never achieve, even if he had thirteen lives to chase after it.
She would wake up smiling, sometimes even laughing, but as much as she would love to know what this Kent Madson was to her, she never seemed to figure it out.
"But aside from that, he is reliable and terrifying."
"Terrifying, how so?" Lady Enyo asked.
"For starters, he is just a Core Formation stage cultivator, but he can easily kill Spirit Lords."
"What?" Both Lady Enyo and the High Priestess exclaimed upon hearing Adina’s words.
"He is dangerous. In fact, before I parted ways with him, he was planning on killing a Level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage demon.
I don’t know if you have heard of him, the wandering Demon swordsman."
"Wait a minute," The High Priestess raised her finger, unsure if she should deploy me to the Valley of Torture despite Adina telling her not to.
"No need to look shocked, High Priestess. It has been a month already; I am sure he has killed him by now. Trust me, Kent is no simple person.
He is friendly, fierce, and resourceful. For now, you all wouldn’t take my words seriously, but when you meet him, you will understand."
The High Priestess looked at Lady Enyo, who held a smile on her face. "My lady, this Kent Madson sounds a lot like you."
Lady Enyo smirked, "I wasn’t able to kill Spirit Lords when I was at his level, so don’t measure me to him. This Kent Madson sounds more like those freaks in the Supreme Worlds and Immortal Worlds."
"Well, he said he is from a washout Medium world. So I think measuring him to them is an insult to Kent. If he were born in such worlds, then he would already be killing gods."
"Looks like you and this Kent are rather close," Lady Enyo spoke with a teasing smile, causing Adina to blush. The High Priestess smiled, watching this.
’At least she is smiling. This is a good thing.’
Watching the smile on Lady Enyo’s face made her very happy. The past few months have been tough.
She was obsessed with Kent Madson to the point that every word that came out of her mouth was all about Kent. However, now, she seemed to have a part of her hunger quenched thanks to Adina.
"What do you plan on doing now, my lady?" The High Priestess asked.
"Nothing. Now that I know he is real, it is only a matter of time before we meet."
The High Priestess sighed, knowing this was indeed a good thing. She wouldn’t have to worry about her for a while, at least.
"Take Adina to the Yin Cave and have her cultivate there. I will handle some issues here, then I will come out of seclusion to help you handle the issues you are facing."
The High Priestess nodded and left with Adina.
When they were gone, Lady Enyo smiled weakly.
"Kent Madson, a beautiful name."
With that, she entered a room to freshen up and then decided on what to handle next. Knowing Adina had spent days with Kent meant she would have some excuse to learn more about him.
[Planet Menelaus – Kent’s POV]
Kent appeared in front of a small stream housing some small medicinal fish. He quickly used the Soul Map to scan his surroundings.
"There is a city east of here. I can see a road with major activities on it leading there," Kent said, and then started walking in that direction.
However, the tower made him stop in his tracks.

[The master must first disguise himself. Interacting with many people runs the risk of having your face out there. You are not at the stage to face immortals and gods, so a disguise will be appropriate.]

Kent knew the tower was right, so he activated the ’Perfect Disguise’ skill and turned into Jest. However, instead of hanging a sword on his back or waist, he bought a fan from the tower and started fanning himself.
[How is the master presenting himself?] Even the tower was taken aback.
Kent smiled, "You can call me Lord Jest, the Everlasting Healer..."

"What was he like?" Lady Enyo asked.
Adina smiled, "Shameless.
That is the best way I can describe him.
That shameless bastard."

For some strange reason, Lady Enyo smiled, recalling some moment in her dream where this Kent Madson would beat his chest and brag about something he could never achieve, even if he had thirteen lives to chase after it.
She would wake up smiling, sometimes even laughing, but as much as she would love to know what this Kent Madson was to her, she never seemed to figure it out.
"But aside from that, he is reliable and terrifying."
"Terrifying, how so?" Lady Enyo asked.
"For starters, he is just a Core Formation stage cultivator, but he can easily kill Spirit Lords."
"What?" Both Lady Enyo and the High Priestess exclaimed upon hearing Adina’s words.
"He is dangerous.
In fact, before I parted ways with him, he was planning on killing a Level 2 Heavenly Ascension stage demon.
I don’t know if you have heard of him, the wandering Demon swordsman."
"Wait a minute," The High Priestess raised her finger, unsure if she should deploy me to the Valley of Torture despite Adina telling her not to.
"No need to look shocked, High Priestess.
It has been a month already; I am sure he has killed him by now.
Trust me, Kent is no simple person.
He is friendly, fierce, and resourceful.
For now, you all wouldn’t take my words seriously, but when you meet him, you will understand."
The High Priestess looked at Lady Enyo, who held a smile on her face.
"My lady, this Kent Madson sounds a lot like you."
Lady Enyo smirked, "I wasn’t able to kill Spirit Lords when I was at his level, so don’t measure me to him.
This Kent Madson sounds more like those freaks in the Supreme Worlds and Immortal Worlds."
"Well, he said he is from a washout Medium world.
So I think measuring him to them is an insult to Kent.
If he were born in such worlds, then he would already be killing gods."
"Looks like you and this Kent are rather close," Lady Enyo spoke with a teasing smile, causing Adina to blush.
The High Priestess smiled, watching this.
’At least she is smiling.
This is a good thing.’
Watching the smile on Lady Enyo’s face made her very happy.
The past few months have been tough.
She was obsessed with Kent Madson to the point that every word that came out of her mouth was all about Kent.
However, now, she seemed to have a part of her hunger quenched thanks to Adina.
"What do you plan on doing now, my lady?" The High Priestess asked.
"Nothing.
Now that I know he is real, it is only a matter of time before we meet."
The High Priestess sighed, knowing this was indeed a good thing.
She wouldn’t have to worry about her for a while, at least.
"Take Adina to the Yin Cave and have her cultivate there.
I will handle some issues here, then I will come out of seclusion to help you handle the issues you are facing."
The High Priestess nodded and left with Adina.
When they were gone, Lady Enyo smiled weakly.
"Kent Madson, a beautiful name."
With that, she entered a room to freshen up and then decided on what to handle next.
Knowing Adina had spent days with Kent meant she would have some excuse to learn more about him.
[Planet Menelaus – Kent’s POV]
Kent appeared in front of a small stream housing some small medicinal fish.
He quickly used the Soul Map to scan his surroundings.
"There is a city east of here.
I can see a road with major activities on it leading there," Kent said, and then started walking in that direction.
However, the tower made him stop in his tracks.
[The master must first disguise himself.
Interacting with many people runs the risk of having your face out there.
You are not at the stage to face immortals and gods, so a disguise will be appropriate.]
Kent knew the tower was right, so he activated the ’Perfect Disguise’ skill and turned into Jest.
However, instead of hanging a sword on his back or waist, he bought a fan from the tower and started fanning himself.
[How is the master presenting himself?] Even the tower was taken aback.
Kent smiled, "You can call me Lord Jest, the Everlasting Healer..."

chapters.title: Chapter 881: Jest, the Everlasting Healer
paragraphs: [May I ask why the master chose to disguise himself as a healer? Not that I doubt the master’s abilities as a healer, but I do want to know why the master picked this path.]
The tower was puzzled to the point it had to ask. Kent becoming a healer was one it wasn’t looking forward to.
Kent smiled. "To answer your question, why don’t you scan the people currently heading to the city?"
The tower did, and for a moment, there was nothing until a sudden discovery made it see Kent in a new light.
[The majority of them are healers and scholars.]

"Indeed. After I formed my core, I was able to scan anyone within an 80,000 km radius. That was why I knew the city I was going to may be one frequented by healers. And since I want to blend in, I chose to disguise myself as one.
Of course, I have some knowledge to pass as a healer, so this is perhaps the best time to become an Alchemist/healer."
[The master never ceases to astonish me.]
Kent smiled and then, with a nonchalant step, he left the stream and started heading toward the city.
The city he was heading to is called Miracle City. It is the fourth largest city on Planet Menelaus.
"Looks like this planet is like one big empire ruled by an empress." Kent used his enchanted eyes to get a general idea of the world as he moved in the direction of Miracle City.

"There are 25 cities in total, with the majority being cities of mercenaries. In fact, now that I have this information, it’s clear that this world is a mercenary-dominated one. Even among the 25 kings and queens, 80% are mercenaries.
Although they don’t take missions anymore, they still support some of the top mercenary teams."
Kent delved deeper into the information on mercenaries and discovered that the ones he killed weren’t exactly the top on Planet Menelaus.
In fact, the ones he killed were among the medium-tier mercenaries.
"Looks like even Iver wasn’t sure of the dynamics in this world. But who could blame him? The world is too big to know everything.
[Maybe even he doesn’t know the affairs of his own world, considering this world is run from revenue generated from mercenary work.
The empress may, in a way, have her way of keeping things confidential, so you knowing this thanks to your enchanted eyes might be regarded as a breach of that confidentiality.]
"I suppose that is a unique take on things." Kent went deeper into the information he had on Planet Menelaus, and after finding all there was to see, he was ready to face anything.
"I should perhaps keep a low profile, considering there is a Level 8 Heavenly Ascension stage Empress and even hidden monsters ready to act."
[The master indeed needs to keep a low profile. After all, gods want you, perhaps even the supremes.]
"Indeed."
Kent quickly appeared on the main road, where he saw some people riding carriages in front of him and others walking.
He kept his nonchalant steps and soon caught up with those ahead.
He didn’t get too close but was close enough to hear what they were saying without using the soul map.

"Looks like this time around, something big has happened in Miracle City. To think every healer in this world and neighboring worlds will be congregating here all of a sudden," one person said, perhaps a guard, considering his friend was wearing the same uniform.
"I suppose you are right. Even the lord sent his youngest son to check out what was happening."
"I just hope it isn’t something tragic like the last time when the King of Hummingbird City was poisoned."
The more they talked, the better Kent understood what might be the issue. Eventually, he caught up to them.

Kent knew talking to them wasn’t going to be too hard, so he asked a question, "Hi brothers, I couldn’t help but overhear your conversation. I would like to know if something dangerous is happening in the city."
Kent put on a concerned face, making sure his aura leaked to tell the two Spirit King guards he was worried about his safety.
They looked at him, and while he expected them to act cocky and perhaps ridicule him for his weaker cultivation base, they instead smiled at him.
"Little brother shouldn’t be worried. Miracle City is one of the safest places in the world. If you are concerned about your safety, then you shouldn’t be."
Kent sighed, feeling relieved. "I suppose I will walk behind you two big brothers just in case."
The two guards laughed, "Suit yourself. But who is this little brother, and where did you come from?"
’I need a world ASAP.’
[The master is from Planet Hecate. It is one of the low-standing worlds in the same planetary alliance that this world is in.]
Kent smiled and replied to the two guards, "My name is Jest. I am from Hecate. My master thought I had learned enough, so he sent me to a random world to gain real-world experience.
This is my first time in this world."

"Oh, that is perfectly understood. Most masters do that to their disciples, and well, it seems your master has some foresight in sending you here. This world is full of talent, and knowing what I know, you will gain a ton of experience here."
Kent smiled, "Looking forward to it."
"Is this little brother, Jest, looking to join a mercenary team?" one of the guards asked, but Kent shook his head.
"I am a healer, so I don’t suppose joining a mercenary team will be ideal for me. I am the type who hates violence."
Right when Kent said that, the window of the carriage swung open, and a young man stuck his head out.
It took Kent a single glance to know the kind of character the young man possessed.
He smiled at Kent, "You should probably talk to my father. I always tell him violence is not the way, but those brutes, they just go around killing as a form of resolving things."
Kent smiled, "May I know who this esteemed scholar is?"

His tone was polite and calm to the point that if someone told you he had just killed dozens of beasts and mercenary teams, even to the point that the infamous wandering demon swordsman fell to his sword, you wouldn’t believe it.
The young man smiled, sensing the scholarlike tone Kent used to ask the question, "You can call me Ander, last born son of the lord of Basel City, King Basel VIII. I am an Array King."
"Well, I am Jest, a Life Saint."
Ander smiled and opened the door of the carriage, "If brother Jest doesn’t mind, I would like to share a ride with him and pick his brain on some things."
Kent smiled and then climbed into the carriage, knowing this was the polite way to get what he wanted, which was to enter the city without having to bribe the guards.
After all, he didn’t have an identification badge, and he wasn’t planning on using the pill badge he received from Pill Monarch Nefeli over 300,000 years ago.
After an hour, they approached the magnificent city built using jade and shining like the night sky.

chapters.title: Chapter 882: Miracle City, The Quest
paragraphs: "This place is beautiful," Kent said as they approached the grand city gate.
It stood 4 km tall with the frame made purely out of gold, and the main gate was also made from an enchanted metal.
The guards standing at the gate wore golden armor forged from one of the most durable metals in the universe.
Kent scanned the surroundings, and all he could see was beauty and luxury. He made the tower start taking note of the architecture and design for when he would be building his next city.
Ander studied Kent’s expression and smile. He knew Kent was indeed new to this place, and that alone made him trust him even more.
He had a good time chatting with Kent on the way to Miracle City, so seeing this side of him made him see Kent in a new light.
"I am sure you would love this place, Jest. The city has more than enough to offer, and as a first-timer on Planet Menelaus, you couldn’t have picked a better city to appear in."
Kent smiled. "I should thank my master for sending me here, then."
"Don’t worry, you will get more than enough things to buy gifts to thank your master when you get back."
"I am looking forward to that."
Kent smiled and then looked out the window, noting the two guards outside had long approached the city guards at the gate and were sorting things out with them.
"Don’t worry. Since you are with me, they will allow us to enter without any trouble."
True to his words, when the guards returned, they started leading the carriage inside. Soon, they passed through the grand tall gate and entered the city.
The moment they entered, Kent felt the healing and unique smell of medicinal essence assault his nose.
"Haha," Ander smiled. "Miracle City—just breathing the air is enough to heal and calm your stressed body down."
The city is filled with healers, and the most common commodity transported there is herbs, so there is always the scent of medicine in the air.

Just by breathing it, one might find the cure for their sickness. It is even common for most cultivators to come to high cultivation rooms to cultivate the medicine since it heals and strengthens them.
"The king in this city is a Life Emperor whose healing abilities are out of this world. He can heal almost any sickness he sets his sight on.
In fact, he has already been recognized as the King of Life by the Empress, the supreme ruler of this world. This recognition alone makes him one of the most respected kings in this world."
Ander was in the sharing mood, so he started giving Kent some information as they rode the carriage into the city, passing by many stores, restaurants, inns, and more.
The stores mainly sell healing herbs.

Kent, who has a wife whose healing magic had already reached the Sage level—just two levels away from reaching the Life Emperor stage—smiled, knowing that if he wanted, he could just ask her a thing or two, just so he could have a good time while in Miracle City.
After all, he planned to relax and have some fun in this Miracle City.
Kent looked at Ander and smiled. "Thank you for telling me this. If possible, I would love to at least see this king before leaving for the next kingdom."
Ander nodded, though he knew telling Kent his dreams might not come to pass would be too harsh, so he merely smiled.
"I will be heading to the Array Headquarters to handle some business. And then I will go to the healing Guild to handle yet another business"
"In that case, you can drop me off at the nearest restaurant." Ander nodded and took out a communication tablet, handing it to Kent.
"You can reach me on that whenever you come to Basel City." After a few minutes’ ride, Kent found himself standing in front of a restaurant.
"Happy Day Restaurant, huh?" Kent smiled and then decided to grab a bite before figuring out his next move.
He was in this world to deliver the wandering Demon Swordman’s head to the Olive Sword Guild in Lison City, the capital of Planet Menelaus.
However, since he wanted to have some fun, he planned to at least get a feel of this world before getting back to the sect.
After all, he planned on knowing something about this world before sending Old Sword, his sworn brother, over.
The moment Kent entered the restaurant, a lady approached him with a polite smile. "Welcome, young man. How may we be of service?"
Kent smiled. "It is my first time in this city, so I plan on enjoying the dishes at the top of your menu."
"Hehe, a food enthusiast, I see. In that case, follow me to the best table we have. Since you want our best, we might as well set you at the best table."
Kent didn’t want to say it, but the lady was a charmer. Kent’s smile widened. "Who am I to turn down such an offer from a beauty such as yourself?"
She led Kent through rows of tables to a corner table where he could overhear everything without looking too suspicious.
"We will be here with your orders soon. For now, enjoy this freshly juiced drink from freshly picked berries personally attended to and grown by a Life King."
Kent nodded and took a sip of the berry juice, making sure he savored the taste like a food critic. A smile appeared on his face, making the lady smile back and walk away.
A few seconds after she left, Kent opened the Soul Map, restricting it to only the restaurant.
He looked at everything happening, but his attention was immediately drawn to a conversation between two slightly older men eating a plate of roasted pork.
"I can’t believe over ten thousand healers and Enigmancers couldn’t solve the Puzzle posted by the Life Emperor," one said.

"I know, right? The last time the Life King set a puzzle was when those bandits poisoned the King of Huckby City. But even back then, he managed to find someone whose knowledge was enough for the task in just two weeks.
However, it has already been three months, and nobody has been able to solve it. At this rate, I’m not sure anyone will be able to solve it."

"Very sad. The Life Emperor is someone who specializes in healing magic, not puzzles. If he had the means, I’m sure he wouldn’t have even put up a puzzle calling all Healers and Enigmancers from the Alliance planets."
As if that was enough for Kent, the tower beeped, signaling a quest. Kent smiled slightly, pulling the details.
⟦You have received a new Chain Quest⟧
⟦First Quest Name: Solve the Unsolvable Puzzle⟧
⟦Quest Type: Chain Quest (1/2)⟧
⟦Quest Difficulty: Hard⟧
↠ It had already been three months since Life Emperor Hael put up the unsolvable puzzle. However, despite many attempts, nobody has been able to solve it.
↠ What many don’t know is that time is running out, and if the puzzle is not solved in the next three days, something bad will happen.
↠ Your quest is to solve the puzzle and then proceed with whatever will come next.
⟦Quest Reward⟧
↠ 100 million Tower Points
↠ Memory Key (Jest)
↠ Memory Key (Faceless Assassin)
⟦Main Reward⟧
↠ Jade Token
"Looks like another requirement for my Sword Sage trial has presented itself," Kent smiled. A few seconds later, his food was served, and he started to dig in as he pondered what he must do next.

A few seconds later, his food was served, and he started to dig in as he pondered what he must do next.

chapters.title: Chapter 883: The Puzzle
paragraphs: As everyone discussed various topics among themselves, with the most important being the Puzzle set by the Life Emperor, Kent happily ate like a king.
Of course, he deserves to eat like a king. Being pulled away only to find himself facing Spirit Lords and even a Heavenly Ascension stage experts was more than enough for a kid like him.

"I can’t believe you left us for a High world and are even enjoying the best delicacies they have to offer. You even dare to tease us about it. Do you think we can’t crash your party?" Vexthra spoke with a slight laugh at the end.
"Yes. We can totally come crash your party," Unity said, also smiling.
"Just say the word, and I will create a mess for him." Selene was ready, as were the rest of her brothers.
Kent smiled as he bit into a chunk of meat. He was talking to his ladies through the harem connection.
[What could possibly go wrong? Oh, let me guess. Out of nowhere, a bunch of heaven-defying beauties appear out of thin air and start causing trouble.
News will spread like fire soon, reaching the Heavenly Ascension stage monsters hidden in the city. They will come out, and when they see a bunch of harmless beauties, they will get the wrong idea.

One thing will lead to another, and I’ll be forced to fight them, which I can totally handle. In the end, after killing a couple of them, my perfect healer disguise will be branded a wanted criminal, and I won’t be able to come to this world, the planetary alliance it is in, or even the star system altogether.
I mean, what could possibly go wrong?]
Vexthra and her sisters smirked, hearing his bragging.

He had already bragged to them about the Spirit Lord beasts he had killed, and while he provided evidence of his remarkable feat, they knew that when it came to Heavenly Ascension stage humanoids, he was out of his league.
He killed one before, but can he kill another while surrounded by dozens of them?
"Sounds like you are having fun," Vexthra said.
[More than you can think, and don’t worry, when I get to the capital, I will bring you guys to have some fun around.]
"That is why you are the best," Camilla laughed and quickly entered the tower to prepare.
They were planning on climbing to the 4th floor of the dungeon soon, but it seemed they would have to put a pin in that for now.
"Just be careful out there. It is a new ascended world, but even so, beings from Great High worlds aren’t as simple as those from Legacy or Low ones."
Vexthra, being the ever-caring wife, made sure his man understood caution.
Kent smiled, drinking juice.
[I will be sure to live like a chicken, keeping my head down always. After all, I am but a humble healer sent by my master to gain some experience in the world out there.]
"Tch, how shameless," Selene chuckled, then added the most important message. "Be sure to keep the dragon in your pants, or else the next time I see you, I will cut it off."
Kent almost choked on his food, but he managed to smile it off. The ladies looked at the Sword Saintess, who shrugged and also entered the tower to prepare.
[Talk to you ladies later.]
Kent cut the connection and focused on his food.
After establishing his connection with the ladies after he had sent Adina away, he exaggerated his feats to them. He even sent the body of one of the beasts he killed, shocking them greatly.

Of course, the ladies panicked when they learned their man was away fighting beasts several realms above his own. They took their time to tell him how precious life is, so he shouldn’t throw his own away.
Ever since then, they have remained in contact until Kent informed them that he had moved to a High world, where life is good and no dangers lurk around every corner.
After finishing his food, the overly enthusiastic lady brought his bill. Kent looked at the bill and smiled. "For such a delicacy, it isn’t even that expensive."
He retrieved a pouch containing spirit stones and handed it to the lady. "You can keep the change." With that, he walked away.

The lady, after watching Kent leave, looked into the pouch, and for a moment, she froze. But then a smile appeared on her lips as she put away the pouch, retrieving only the right amount for the bill.
As the saying goes, your life changer might be a handsome dude dressed in black with an appetite for any food.
Kent left the store, spreading his Soul Map.
In a minute, he was seeing the 80,000 km radius of the city. Though the city is several times bigger than that, he was able to find what he was looking for within the coverage of his Soul Map.
He quickly made his way to the Healing Guild, where he could see major activity happening. After a few minutes of walking, he appeared in front of a green pagoda.
It has seven floors, and on the ground floor, hundreds of people were gathered around a stone tablet.
As Kent slowly approached the tablet, he picked up on the whispers among the people standing around.

"It is just too bad nobody was able to figure out the puzzle. Not even Lord Abass was able to handle it this time, despite having a winning streak of solving almost all puzzles in the Alliance," one person said with a sigh.
Another person also sighed and said, "It isn’t always the case that nobody in the world and even the Alliance could solve such a problem. I mean, what would be the implication this time around?
The last time, King Hap nearly lost his son when he was almost stuck in the Puzzle Space."
Kent could see the concerned look on their faces. It was like their failure was the recipe for disaster.
Of course, Kent saw from the quest that if he were unable to solve the puzzle in three days, something bad would happen.
So he walked past them and slowly approached the tablet. After deactivating the Soul Map, he only saw the three boxes inside the three glass boxes when he was a few steps in front of the tablet.
’Three boxes placed inside three glass boxes.’
Kent stopped and examined the glass boxes, and as expected, there was a lock formation on them.
He also saw 15 people seated a few steps away from the stone tablet and three boxes, each focusing intently on the three puzzles.
Looking away from them, he stared at the stone tablet.

Kent’s eyes scanned the stone tablet, where three riddles were etched in a runic inscription. It was a language only a few can decipher. However, from the way people were talking, most can read it perfectly.
The puzzle was a test of logic and perception. It has three separate challenges, each holding the key to open the glass boxes. To unlock the boxes, one had to solve all three puzzles correctly.
The first puzzle read:
"Invisible threads bind the unseen,
Connecting all yet touching none.
I hold the past and shape the future,
Yet I have no form, no weight, no breath.
What am I?"
The second puzzle:
"I move without legs,
Carry without arms,
I am endless yet confined,
You cannot hold me, but I hold all.
What am I?"
The third puzzle was:
"Born from chaos, I dance in silence,
Neither living nor dead,
I consume without hunger,
And vanish with a single drop.
What am I?"
A couple of meters away, a young man’s eyes lit up when he saw Kent. This young man, of course, is Ander, the scholar dude who gave Kent a ride to the city.

chapters.title: Chapter 884: Solving The Puzzle, Danger
paragraphs: If today happened to be the day the puzzle was displayed, many would have insulted or outright killed Kent when he moved forward, showing he was also here to solve the puzzle.
As a Core Formation stage cultivator, he had no business coming near something that Spirit Lords and a few Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators couldn’t solve.
In fact, his mere presence wouldn’t have managed to make it 2km from the tablet when it was first put up.
However, it had already been three months, and nobody was able to solve the puzzle.
Just that failure was enough for Kent to face no insults when he approached the tablet.
However, as the weakest to have walked forward, looking to solve the puzzle, everyone had their eyes on him, including a few powerful ones sitting at the 7th level, the highest floor of the pagoda.
At the peak of the pagoda sat a Level 6 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator and two others who also had cultivations at the Heavenly Ascension stage but paled in comparison to the first person.
This person was, of course, Life Emperor Hael, and the two, also Life Emperors, were his immediate subordinates: Life Emperor Kac and Phub.
Life Emperor Hael is the King/Lord of Miracle City.
"Who is that kid?" Life Emperor Kac watched Kent walk and sit down among the fifteen, still doing their best to solve the puzzle.
"I have no idea," Life Emperor Phub answered, "But why? It isn’t like he is breaking any rule."
"Of course, I know he isn’t breaking any rules. It is just that a Core Formation cultivator joining the ranks of Spirit Ascension stage and above feels more like an insult to me."

"Where is the insult in this? It has already been three months, and not even the best Enigmancer was able to solve this damn puzzle. If that isn’t enough of an insult to us all, then I don’t know what an insult is."
Life Emperor Kac sighed in his heart, knowing what Life Emperor Phub said was indeed true. It isn’t pleasant, but true to the last dot.
"Just where did this puzzle come from, and why was it addressed to us?" Life Emperor Phub wondered, already concluding that soon, something bad would happen if the puzzle wasn’t solved.
Life Emperor Hael sat there, watching as everyone came and failed to solve the puzzle.
Meanwhile, Kent sat there with a calm expression, looking at the stone tablet.
’First of all, this isn’t a puzzle but a riddle,’ Kent sighed in his heart, knowing that the moment things switched from puzzle to riddle, the outcome became one that couldn’t easily be determined.

Puzzles are mostly easy to solve simply because a puzzle is a problem that, to some extent, requires physical interaction to solve. In most cases, a trial-and-error approach often leads to the person finding the solution to the puzzle.
At least, that was his take on puzzles from his Earth Knowledge.
But with riddles, it is virtually impossible to do trial and error.
Kent smiled slightly, making sure nobody saw it, for he could already sense powerful people beyond his strength level keeping close eyes on him.

’The second thing is, for a cultivation world where there are no schools, these riddles are things that require great thinking and problem-solving skills. However, to someone like me who has a PhD in computer science and cybersecurity, this riddle is child’s play to me.’
Kent cast his mind back to his life on Earth.
He became one of the few young people to earn a PhD, largely because his life was too dull and he had no active social life.
His first 25 years were spent on his books, earning many degrees that in the end he didn’t use. Instead, he became a movie director.
’I was boring and a nerd back then, but who would have thought it would help me today?’
This time, the smile on his face caught the attention of others, making them wonder if Kent had solved the puzzle.
Naturally, they were all leaning toward the positive side of things because if he turned out to be one of those who failed, people would find an excuse to make his life feel a little tight.
Kent looked at the first riddle.
’Invisible threads bind the unseen, connecting all yet touching none. I hold the past and shape the future,’ Kent scoffed.
’That is clearly Time.’
’They couldn’t have found something more complex to challenge me.’ Kent focused on the second riddle and scoffed again, feeling a pride he never knew he had been insulted by these easy riddles.
’I move without legs, carry without arms, I am endless yet confined.’ Kent paused and smirked, ’What else would be the answer if not a River?’
’Born from chaos, I dance in silence, neither living nor dead, I consume without hunger.’ He smirked again. ’We both know the answer is fire.’
Kent shook his head, stood up, and started walking toward the three glass boxes.
"What is he doing?" one of the people seated and trying to solve the puzzles asked, looking at Kent.
"Did he solve it?" another said, and soon, everyone started wondering the same thing.

"Brother Jest, show them what true talent looks like," Ander, who saw an opportunity to make a name for himself, shouted Kent’s name. Kent, of course, stopped, turned, and looked at him and smiled before he resumed his journey.
He knew what Ander wanted, and so he gave it to him. Making a name off Kent’s name wasn’t something he minded. After all, he owned Ander for that ride to Miracle City.
After a few steps, Kent arrived before the three glass boxes. There was a spirit brush on the stand where the three boxes were placed.
He picked it up and channeled his energy into it.
At this point, everyone was looking dead serious at Kent. Even the Life Emperors on the top floor of the pagoda were also paying close attention.
Kent, after pouring his energy into the brush, started to write the answers in runic language, just like how the riddles were written.
In the first box, he wrote Time. On the second, he wrote River, and on the third, Fire.
Right when Kent wrote the third answer, a formation appeared from the ground, and then slowly, the three glasses cracked and dissipated into thin air.
The three boxes were revealed, inciting gasps and shocked expressions from everyone.
The three Life Emperors appeared at the same time, just a few meters away from the boxes. They landed on the ground and walked toward the boxes.
Kent set the brush down and then looked at the boxes.
However, he didn’t get a chance to pay closer attention since the three Life Emperors appeared before him, blocking his view.
"Who might this little brother be?" Like he hadn’t complained a few minutes ago, Life Emperor Kac asked with a smile.
Kent looked at him and then at the two beside him. "I am Jest, a Life Saint."

The three Life Emperors looked at Kent with some form of respect. Of course, they held respectful gazes because they were truly surprised a mere Core Formation cultivator was able to do what many couldn’t.
"Uhm, seniors, if you don’t mind, I have to solve the puzzle on the boxes. Each of the three contains a message, I believe, and until all three boxes are opened, we wouldn’t know what is inside."
The three Life Emperors looked surprised, hearing there was another puzzle. However, hearing what Kent said, they stepped aside to let him handle the puzzle.

chapters.title: Chapter 885: The Three True Puzzles
paragraphs: The three Life Emperors didn’t even want to question Kent at the moment.
The puzzle they had received—and which they themselves had spent three weeks trying to solve but couldn’t—before putting it out to the entire world, was just solved by a junior.
If there was no reason to give Kent face, then this feat alone was enough to earn their respect and prevent them from questioning anything he says.
Thus, they allowed him to move toward the boxes.
Kent, meanwhile, held a puzzled look in his eyes as he walked toward the three boxes.
’So this was what the quest was referring to as the puzzles. The riddle was just the appetizer for the main dish.’
⟦All the master has to do is place his hand on the various boxes, and the puzzle to solve would be revealed. It will appear as if you’re learning a new skill or technique.⟧
Kent smiled and stood before the first box, placing his hand on it. The moment his hand touched it, his consciousness was pulled into the space where the puzzle was to be solved.
Kent’s senses sharpened as he was drawn deeper into the puzzle’s realm. It was as if his mind was focused intently on the puzzle, with nothing else on his mind.
The surroundings shifted into a serene forest clearing bathed in soft, golden light. Ancient trees towered overhead, their leaves whispering as a cold breeze blew past them.
In the center lay a circle of stones, each inscribed with unfamiliar runes glowing faintly.
"Looks like that is the puzzle to be solved," Kent muttered as he walked closer to get a better view. He noticed his soul map and other abilities weren’t working in the puzzle realm.
However, in a strange way he couldn’t understand, his mind was brought to its full capacity by just appearing in this realm.

The moment Kent appeared before the stones, a voice echoed softly in his mind: "To unlock the truth, master the harmony of the elements. Align the stones in the order of creation’s birth, or be lost to the eternal forest."
Kent’s pupils shrank for a moment before a smile appeared on his face.
Kent knelt, studying the runes carefully. He recognized symbols representing earth, water, fire, air, and spirit. The puzzle demanded not brute strength, but understanding.
He must gain an attunement to the natural flow.
"There was nothing, but then he created the heavens and the earth."
Slowly, Kent reached out, touching the stone marked with earth. It pulsed warmly beneath his fingers.
He was asked to solve the puzzle by aligning the five elements in the order of Creation’s birth. Just so it happened, Kent is from Earth, where life and everything it contains were created.
Thus, he knew what had to come first.
"Water covered the surface of the entire earth."
Next, he moved to water, feeling a cool ripple.
"Then the water was separated, making way for mountains and trees." Kent smiled, "With trees, there can be Fire."
The next stone he touched was Fire, which emitted a spark of energy.
He followed up with Air, which danced lightly, and finally, Spirit glowed softly.
As he placed the stones in sequence — earth, water, fire, air, spirit — a harmonious chime filled the clearing.
The runes flared brighter, and the circle of stones began to dissolve, revealing a glowing key hovering above the ground.

Kent took the key, and then he was back outside, now holding a glowing key. When the Life Emperors saw this, they were yet again struck with another shock, seeing Kent solve a puzzle they knew came with a realm within mere minutes.
They knew that puzzles that require one to enter a puzzle realm to solve are complex and, in most cases, require several months, some even years, to solve. However, Kent solved it in mere minutes.
Under their watchful gaze, Kent moved and touched the second box.
Just like what happened with the first box, he was pulled into the puzzle realm, appearing in front of three mirrors.
His reflection appeared inside each mirror, mirroring his posture and movements.
"One must know their true self and recognize their true reflection. The mirrors show what one wants to see, but can you spot who you are?"
The voice spoke again, revealing the purpose of the second puzzle.
"I must figure out which is my true self, and there is only one correct answer." Kent sighed. "Who knows what will happen if I choose the wrong one?"
Kent paid close attention to the mirrors, looking intently at his reflections. A few minutes into the process, Kent noticed something that made him raise his brow.
"The mirrors show what one wants to see." The sentence clearly said the mirror would show him what he wanted to see. So, it means that if he wills it, the mirror will show him what he wants to see.
"I want to see the real me."
The mirrors flickered, and the reflections on them changed. They now stood still, staring at Kent with eyes that said so many things.
"Creepy." The moment Kent met the gaze of the first reflection in the first mirror, he felt like a creep was staring at him. This made him smirk, then focus on the second reflection.
"My true self cannot be a creep."
The second reflection, however, held a look of calm, peace, and tranquility.
"Tch, a goody two-shoes." Kent laughed, unsure why something this bland was staring at him. He didn’t know why, but looking at the second reflection made him see the opposite of himself.
However, when he stared at the third reflection, he also felt that the evil and sadistic eyes looking at him could not be his.
"The mirrors show what one wants to see, yet I see not what I wanted." Kent backed away and turned his back on the three mirrors.

"One is whole, one is unchanged, thus one cannot have a true reflection," Kent spoke the words, then he turned and faced the mirrors. "None is my reflection because all is my reflection. I pick none."
The mirrors hummed, then cracked, dispersing into specks of red, blue, and white light.
In their place, a shining golden key appeared.
Kent grabbed it, and then he was back outside, shocking everyone.
Everyone kept wondering just where this youngster came from, for the brilliance he was showing was one that nobody could understand.
However, while they were all wondering that, Kent walked to the third box and placed his hand on it. This time, he appeared before a river.
The water was blue, and there were small stones, jade white, lining the bank of the river.
Lying before him was a stone colored blue with runic markings all over it. He picked up the stone
"The stone of gods, the everlasting embrace of the light. The sea flows against the tide..." The voice paused, allowing Kent to continue the statement.
The last puzzle was about him completing the markings on the stone.
A smile appeared on Kent’s face, recalling a famous quote he once read from a humanitarian’s memoir back on Earth.
"And the wave comes to shore," Kent ended the statement. The stone in his hand shone, and the third key appeared in his hand.
He appeared back outside. The moment he opened his eyes, the three keys flew from his hand and unlocked the three boxes, revealing three pieces of a scroll.

chapters.title: Chapter 886: The Cult Of Wisdom
paragraphs: "He actually did. He solved all three puzzles that even well-known Enigmancers couldn’t solve in three months," someone shouted.
Everybody was now looking at the three boxes that were open.
"Who is this kid?" someone else asked.
"Who cares who he is? I just want to know what is written on those scrolls."
Life Emperor Hael, the king or lord of Miracle City, looked at Kent and nodded slightly with a thankful and respectful gaze, then moved toward the open boxes.
However, something strange happened.
Just as he was three steps away from the boxes, a light flashed from the three scrolls, pushing him back.
This startled everyone.
However, the next second, runic markings rose from the scrolls and wrote three words in the air:
"Cult of Wisdom."
The moment people read these words, their faces turned pale, including the Three Life Emperors. Kent, who was standing in front of the scrolls, raised his brow, looking at everyone’s faces.
’What is happening?’ Kent wondered.
He never expected someone who was just a few steps away from reaching the peak of a High world to look pale just from reading three words.
’Who or what is this Cult of Wisdom?’ Kent wondered again, then chose to ask.
"Seniors, why do you all look like you have seen a ghost?"
Life Emperor Hael looked at Kent with a frown for a few seconds before turning back to the three words in the air.
"This is the business of the Cult of Wisdom. When it comes to them, even the Empress would have to lower his head, so how are you still standing?"
Kent raised his brow and turned to look at the three scrolls upon hearing Life Emperor Hael’s words. The scrolls were one but divided into three parts.
Kent picked up the first scroll, then moved to the second and picked it before finally arriving at the third. Everyone looking at him had a calm yet scared look.

The Cult of Wisdom — the one cult that only thirsts after wisdom and would do anything to acquire it. Their legacy is one fraught with evil, for when it comes to acquiring wisdom, they don’t mind killing millions to get it.
Kent merely held a curious look as he pieced the three pieces of the scroll together. The moment he arranged them well, a faint light came from the three pieces of the scrolls, merging them together.
He picked it up and turned to face everyone.
Strangely, Kent felt an external force compel him to read the content of the scroll to everyone.
"This is the Cult of Wisdom. If you are reading this, it means you have passed our trial. Congratulations. However, this is not over.
Ten years from today, the Cult of Wisdom will hold the Trial of Wisdom to pick the bearers of the Ten Seals of Wisdom collected over a span of 7 million years.
This is the invitation to the one who solved the puzzles. You are required to answer the call when the time is due, for this is your destiny.

As a sign of precaution, we have poisoned the ruler of this Alliance and the world. To prove your worth and receive the seal of wisdom, seek the last puzzle, solve it, and you will receive the antidote.
Failure will cause your leader to die along with half the world. And remember, this is the Cult of Wisdom; there is no escaping us."
After reading the content, Kent finally understood why everyone became pale when they saw the name, "Cult of Wisdom."

However, Kent didn’t panic. He looked at a complex puzzle left at the bottom of the scroll. His brain kicked into puzzle-solving mode as he tried to piece the puzzle together. A few minutes later, he figured it out.
At the same time, the quest was updated, giving him the next task. Kent immediately paid attention to it.
⟦Congratulations on completing the first part of the quest. Your rewards have been released⟧
⟦Second Quest⟧
⟦Quest Name: Worthy Candidate of the Cult of Wisdom⟧
⟦Description: Find the last puzzle and solve it to obtain the Seal of Wisdom⟧
⟦Rewards:⟧
↠ 100 Million Tower Points
↠ Memory Key (Chaos)
Life Emperor Hael looked at Kent with a raised brow.
"Come with me," he waved his hand, and Kent felt his body move. The next second, they were several miles away from Miracle City. They stood inside a flying ship large enough to hold many people.

The speed at which it was going was several times faster than Kent could comprehend. In fact, it was going so fast that he wasn’t even willing to consider whether any of his flying treasures could match it.
’I don’t have 80 billion yet, so I can get the divine-grade flying treasures, but I am sure they wouldn’t fly faster than this,’ Kent thought, turning to Life Emperor Hael.
"Where are we going?"
"Lison City to see the Empress."
"Oh. But shouldn’t we be going to Slaxson City instead? It is the location of the next puzzle."
"Are you sure?" Life Emperor Hael asked, and Kent nodded.
Though he still couldn’t truly understand why they feared the Cult of Wisdom so much, he could tell they knew more than he did, and so they were all acting more strangely than usual.

Even so, he also understood that perhaps Life Emperor Hael was just scared for the life of the Empress and half the planet. In fact, news had already spread to many cities, warning them of the danger looming over Planet Manelaus.
However, to Kent, they just had to get the puzzle, and everything would take care of itself. Those already leaving the planet were just overreacting.
Life Emperor Hael turned the ship toward Slaxson City, and they started traveling there.

"We will get the puzzle, and then we will use a teleportation gate to get to Lison City," Life Emperor Hael said, already praying in his heart that things would end up well, that Kent would be able to solve the next puzzle.
If he fails, then the Empress will die and, like the Cult of Wisdom wrote, half of the planet will die with her.
To someone like Kent, who hadn’t encountered the Cult of Wisdom before, it would sound like a joke; however, to them, this was serious.
Kent wanted to strike up a conversation with the Life Emperor, but looking at him pacing back and forth, Kent held back.
The journey to Slaxson City took four hours. By the time they reached 10,000 km from it, three Heavenly Ascension stage experts met them and led them into the city.
News had already reached them, and so they were prepared to receive them.
"This is not how I expected my first day in this world to go," Kent muttered, flying toward a magnificent city made from a strange stone, blending green and blue colors.
"The city lord has already arranged 10,000 mercenaries to help in the search," one of the Heavenly Ascension stage experts said.
Kent looked at them and squinted his eyes.
"No need to use that many people. Just take me to the Grand Mercantile Store; the puzzle is there."
"Are you sure?" the man asked, turning to Life Emperor Hael.
"Listen to him. He was the one who solved the puzzles." Thanks to this reveal, the three Heavenly Ascension stage experts no longer questioned Kent.
They led him toward the direction of the store while Life Emperor Hael followed behind.
